title: What your event platform isn't telling you about its AI features | Zuddl Blog
summary: AI in event management today stops at the feature layer. Here is why fragmented data limits what it can do, and what a unified agentic platform changes.
body_text: In 2026, you can't walk 10 seconds without bumping into something AI. It's there when you open Linkedin. You see it in billboard signs (especially in SF) and when your phone has an update. Every tool you use has it, including event marketing platforms. You've probably been in demos that show you AI session summaries, or email copy that can be whipped up in seconds, or tools that turn session recordings into clips for social media. They're all great and they save time. More or less. Agness Wandavison GIF from Agness GIFs AI features promising to reinvent the way you work ‍ What they don't do is change the workflow underneath it all. The guest list is still a spreadsheet. The lead export will still take two days. The context from the dinner conversation on Thursday night will still get lost by the time it makes it to the CRM. But an AI-first platform can do much more than save a few minutes on individual tasks. What counts as AI in event management today As per a 2025 Soundings survey, 59% of event professionals already use AI, with the majority of them using it for content creation. Most AI in event platforms today shows up in individual features and they are useful in many ways. The problem is that this can't go beyond the feature layer. Most event platforms do not know what an attendee did at your last three events, or where they are in a buying conversation. When the model has no memory of the person, the output can't go beyond a superficial level. An Events Marketing Manager at a B2B software company says, "I think there are opportunities for AI personalization when it comes to our events, but we've only just skimmed the surface." AI is only as powerful as the context you give it. And most event platforms have very little context to give. Why fragmented data makes AI in event management worse The average enterprise event program runs across more tools than the fingers on your hands. Almost two-thirds of marketers use more tools than two years ago. In the case of one field marketing team, their event platform was one of 12 tools they used. Today event teams might work with separate systems for registration, webinars, field events, CRM, marketing automation, lead capture , content, analytics. Each tool does one job and holds one part of the whole information pie. When the data is split that way, there might as well be no AI in your event platform. The attendee who came to your webinar in January and your roadshow in March looks identical to the AI as someone who just registered for the first time. The model cannot distinguish them, and you end up manually tweaking flows and assets every time. This is the reason most event AI does not deliver at the scale it promises. When you have different codebases and databases that have no way to speak to each other, you get automation at most. And automation is not intelligence. The pattern has been documented outside events too. When software teams started using AI coding assistants, individual developers wrote code significantly faster. But the time it actually took to ship finished software barely changed. Faros studied over 10,000 developers and found that review queues got longer while company-level delivery metrics stayed flat. The bottleneck turned out to be everything else in the process. AI in event marketing is in a similar state today. It might help you speed up one thing, but the pipe is still clogged with a spreadsheet waiting for approval, or a sales rep not following up on a good lead. What agentic AI for events actually looks like On the surface, a Zapier-like flow might feel great. For example, if an attendee checks in at the event, send a welcome SMS. If they visit the product demo booth, add them to the high-intent follow-up list. If the event ends and they were marked as "engaged," assign them to the nearest available rep in Salesforce. But this is mechanical. Each step fires because that's what the flow dictates. The logic never changes regardless of who the attendee is or what else you know about them. Agentic AI requires a foundation: a shared data layer across your brand and the events you hold. With that, the platform has enough context to act on. Combine that with some important guardrails, and the AI can now help you at the workflow level. The guest list stops being a spreadsheet that bounces around in discussion threads. An event marketer can just describe what a good guest looks like in plain language, and the platform scores every name against that description, with live CRM data in every row. Approvals happen with deal stage and account context already visible. A VP who used to spend 45 minutes switching between tabs to check each name now looks at a row, sees the context, and decides on nominations. The event marketer is no longer a Slack pinball. Follow-up stops being the event marketer's job. When the event ends, the platform knows which reps were assigned leads and drafts the emails for them. It monitors whether they follow up, and if they haven't, it escalates. Because the platform has context about your brand, you can generate on-brand assets almost immediately. When the session ends, clips and draft posts start generating. Instead of building a post-event report by hand, the platform can show the event marketer drop-off trends, engagement by session, lead quality by event type with a conversational query. That's what an AI-first platform can do. AI should not be a separate feature. When it's built into the platform's foundation, you can look past just speed of output and start taking judgment calls based on the data it shows you. {{demo-widget-1}}

title: Bay Runner Twin: Another feeder for Gulf Coast’s LNG export boom
summary: Enbridge, partners announce pipeline’s sanctioning, Blackcomb commissioning as Permian gas exports ramp up
body_text: Enbridge, partners announce pipeline’s sanctioning, Blackcomb commissioning as Permian gas exports ramp up August 06, 2026 It will potentially be the largest LNG export facility on the Gulf Coast. And today, Enbridge announced details of another conduit to feed its massive projected output. NextDecade’s Rio Grande LNG facility , which expects to ship its first product in 2027, has about 6.3 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d), or 48 million tonnes per annum (mtpa), of LNG export capacity under construction and in development. Five liquefaction trains, or large processing facilities, will convert natural gas to LNG for export via the facility’s two marine berths at the Port of Brownsville, Texas—with further expansion plans in the works that include three more trains and another marine berth. On July 31, as part of Enbridge’s 2026 Q2 earnings call, we announced that the Whistler joint venture partnership—in which we own a 19% stake—has sanctioned the Bay Runner Twin pipeline to deliver Permian natural gas to NextDecade’s Rio Grande LNG facility. You may also like: LNG Exports Flexing North American energy muscle, advancing LNG export capacity Economy Expanded Eiger, supersized Traverse, Matterhorn: Enbridge’s Permian pipeline push continues Energy A prize Permian plan: Our Whistler assets in West Texas Permian gas transmission “is something that we've looked at strategically and advanced very intentionally in the past few years,” said Enbridge’s Matthew Akman, Executive Vice President and President of our Gas Transmission business, said during our Q2 earnings call. Serving additional Rio Grande LNG trains The Bay Runner Twin, to be built in the corridor of the currently-under-construction Bay Runner pipeline, will provide up to 2.6 Bcf/d of incremental capacity between Agua Dulce and Rio Grande. “We’ve officially sanctioned the Bay Runner Twin to service additional trains at Rio Grande LNG,” said Enbridge President and CEO Greg Ebel during our Q2 earnings call. Enbridge also announced on July 31 that the Blackcomb Pipeline, which will move up to 2.5 Bcf/d of gas from the Permian to Agua Dulce, has begun commissioning and will soon enter service and ramp up through the second half of 2026. The Bay Runner and Bay Runner Twin lines are effectively extensions of the operational Whistler Pipeline , a 450-mile line traveling from the Permian to Agua Dulce. Enbridge: A player in Permian gas egress With significant, growing Gulf Coast storage assets and an expanding portfolio of Permian egress pipelines, Enbridge is connected to every operating LNG export facility on the USGC . "(Permian gas transmission) is something that we've looked at strategically and advanced very intentionally in the past few years." Matthew Akman Enbridge Executive Vice President and President, Gas Transmission As part of various partnerships that include WhiteWater/I Squared Capital, MPLX LP, ONEOK Inc. and Targa Resources, Enbridge’s ownership stake in other Texas gas assets includes: The operational 580-mile Matterhorn Express Pipeline (up to 2.5 Bcf/d), which runs from the Permian to Wharton, TX. The Eiger Express Pipeline (up to 3.7 Bcf/d) from the Permian to Katy TX, expected to enter service in mid-2028. The Traverse Pipeline (up to 2.5 Bcf/d of bidirectional service) from Agua Dulce to Katy, which should enter service in 2027. The operational ADCC Pipeline , serving Cheniere’s Corpus Christi LNG export facility. The operational Waha Gas Storage facility which connects to key Permian egress pipelines. The operational Delaware Basin Residue (DBR) pipeline system that supplies the Whistler system.

title: Geron Corporation Reports Inducement Grants Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)
summary: FOSTER CITY, Calif., Aug. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Geron Corporation (Nasdaq: GERN), a commercial stage biopharmaceutical company, today reported that, effective August 17, 2026, it granted stock options to purchase an aggregate of 311,250 shares of common stock to six newly hired employees as
body_text: Geron Corporation Reports Inducement Grants Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4) August 18, 2026 PDF Version FOSTER CITY, Calif., Aug. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Geron Corporation (Nasdaq: GERN), a commercial stage biopharmaceutical company, today reported that, effective August 17, 2026, it granted stock options to purchase an aggregate of 311,250 shares of common stock to six newly hired employees as an inducement material to such employees’ acceptance of employment with Geron. The stock options have an exercise price of $1.53 per share, which is equal to the closing price of Geron’s common stock on the grant date, have a ten-year term and vest over four years, with 12.5% of the shares underlying the options vesting on the six-month anniversary of commencement of employment of such employee and the remaining shares vesting over the following 42 months in equal installments of whole shares, subject to continued employment with Geron through the applicable vesting dates. The equity awards were granted by the Compensation Committee of Geron’s Board of Directors in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4) and are subject to the terms and conditions of Geron’s 2018 Inducement Award Plan and the form of stock option agreement under the plan. About Geron Geron is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company aiming to change lives by changing the course of blood cancer. Our first-in-class telomerase inhibitor RYTELO® (imetelstat) is approved in the United States and the European Union for the treatment of certain adult patients with lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes with transfusion dependent anemia. We are also conducting a pivotal Phase 3 clinical trial of imetelstat in JAK-inhibitor relapsed/refractory myelofibrosis, as well as studies in other hematologic malignancies. Inhibiting telomerase activity, which is increased in malignant stem and progenitor cells in the bone marrow, aims to potentially reduce proliferation and induce death of malignant cells. To learn more, visit www.geron.com or follow us on LinkedIn . CONTACT: Dawn Schottlandt Senior Vice President, Investor Relations and Corporate Affairs dschottlandt@geron.com

title: AWS Config now supports 15 new resource types
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with AWS Config now supports 15 new resource types
body_text: AWS Config now supports 15 new resource types Posted on: Aug 3, 2026 AWS Config now supports 15 additional AWS resource types across key services including Amazon Bedrock, Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, and Amazon SageMaker. This expansion provides greater coverage over your AWS environment, enabling you to more effectively discover, assess, audit, and remediate an even broader range of resources. With this launch, if you have enabled recording for all resource types, then AWS Config will automatically track these new additions. The newly supported resource types are also available in Config rules and Config aggregators. You can now use AWS Config to monitor the following newly supported resource types in all AWS Regions where the resources are available: Resource Types: AWS::AppSync::DomainName AWS::OpenSearchServerless::AccessPolicy AWS::Bedrock::AutomatedReasoningPolicy AWS::OpenSearchServerless::LifecyclePolicy AWS::Bedrock::AutomatedReasoningPolicyVersion AWS::SageMaker::ImageVersion AWS::Bedrock::Blueprint AWS::SageMaker::InferenceComponent AWS::Bedrock::DataAutomationProject AWS::SageMaker::PartnerApp AWS::BedrockAgentCore::ApiKeyCredentialProvider AWS::SageMaker::Project AWS::Connect::UserHierarchyGroup AWS::SageMaker::Space AWS::Glue::Trigger

title: Spotify führt eine neue Kennzeichnung für KI-generierte Künstler*innen-Identitäten ein
summary: Eine echte Verbindung zwischen Künstler*innen und Fans braucht Vertrauen und Authentizität. Gerade im Zeitalter generativer KI müssen Hörer*innen darauf vertrauen können, dass die Künstler*innen hinter der Musik auch diejenigen sind, als die sie sich ausgeben. Deshalb haben wir das Thema „Artist Identity & Trust“ in diesem Jahr zu einer unserer wichtigsten Prioritäten gemacht – mit...
body_text: Eine echte Verbindung zwischen Künstler*innen und Fans braucht Vertrauen und Authentizität. Gerade im Zeitalter generativer KI müssen Hörer*innen darauf vertrauen können, dass die Künstler*innen hinter der Musik auch diejenigen sind, als die sie sich ausgeben. Deshalb haben wir das Thema „Artist Identity & Trust“ in diesem Jahr zu einer unserer wichtigsten Prioritäten gemacht – mit der Einführung von „Von Spotify verifiziert“, „SongDNA“, „KI-Songinfos“ sowie dem Schutz des Künstler*innen-Profils. Heute gehen wir einen weiteren Schritt, um Spotify zu einem möglichst transparenten und vertrauenswürdigen Ort für Musik zu machen. Das Feedback unserer Hörer*innen war klar: Sie wollen erkennen können, ob hinter einem Profil eine reale Person oder eine KI-generierte Persona steht. Deshalb wird ab Mitte September auf ausgewählten Künstler*innen-Profilen ein AI Persona Badge sichtbar. Dieser zeigt Hörer*innen, dass die Identität eines Artists KI-generiert sein kann und keine reale Person repräsentiert. Neben Künstler*innen-Profilen, die ihren Status als AI Persona selbst offenlegen, werden wir auch relevante Profile entsprechend kennzeichnen. Musik von AI Personas wird bei Spotify standardmäßig nicht in redaktionellen oder personalisierten Empfehlungen ausgespielt. Sie taucht nur dann auf, wenn Nutzer*innen einer AI Persona aktiv folgen. Unsere Programmierung konzentriert sich darauf, authentische Künstler*innen zu fördern, die eine Karriere in der Musik aufbauen. Gleichzeitig können Künstler*innen selbst entscheiden, wie sie sich präsentieren. So funktioniert’s Ab heute können Künstler*innen über Spotify for Artists angeben, dass ihr Profil eine AI Persona repräsentiert. Wir setzen auf Transparenz und geben Künstler*innen die Möglichkeit zur Selbstoffenlegung, verlassen uns aber nicht allein darauf. Spotify wird Profile auch eigenständig prüfen und solche identifizieren, die sich über Name und Bildsprache als fotorealistische, KI-generierte Person darstellen. Wir beginnen mit Profilen, die bestimmte Reichweitenschwellen erreicht haben, sodass die Kennzeichnung die große Mehrheit der Profile abdeckt, die Nutzer*innen tatsächlich besuchen. Ab Mitte September werden Hörer*innen das AI Persona Badge auf Künstler*innen-Profilen (im Banner und im Bereich „Infos“), in der Suche sowie bei Tracks in Playlists sehen. Beim Antippen des Badges können Hörer*innen erkennen, ob Künstler*innen den eigenen AI-Persona-Status selbst offengelegt haben oder ob Spotify das Profil geprüft und eine entsprechende Einschätzung vorgenommen hat. Künstler*innen, deren Profil nach einer Prüfung durch Spotify gekennzeichnet wurde, werden informiert und erhalten die Möglichkeit, ihren Status selbst offenzulegen oder Einspruch einzulegen. In den kommenden Monaten werden wir Hörer*innen außerdem die Möglichkeit geben, Künstler*innen-Profile zu melden, bei denen sie eine AI Persona vermuten. Weitere Details dazu teilen wir, sobald die Funktion verfügbar ist. Künstler*innen setzen KI als kreatives Werkzeug auf ganz unterschiedliche Weise ein. Das AI Persona Badge schafft Klarheit darüber, ob ein Profil eine reale Person repräsentiert. Es bezieht sich auf die öffentliche Identität eines Artists, nicht darauf, wie die Musik entstanden ist. Für Transparenz zum Entstehungsprozess bieten wir KI-Songinfos und SongDNA . Schon bei den KI-Songinfos sehen wir, dass viele Künstler*innen diese Möglichkeit aktiv nutzen. Wir hoffen auf eine ähnlich hohe Bereitschaft bei AI Personas. Mehr Vertrauen und Transparenz auf Spotify AI Persona Badges sind Teil unserer umfassenderen Arbeit, Spotify zu einem möglichst transparenten und vertrauenswürdigen Ort für Musik zu machen. 2026 haben wir mehrere weitere Funktionen eingeführt, die Hörer*innen mehr Transparenz darüber geben, was sie hören und wer dahintersteht: „Von Spotify verifiziert“ zeigt Hörer*innen, dass hinter einem Künstler*innen-Profil eine reale Person steht, die sich authentisch auf Spotify präsentiert. KI-Songinfos ermöglichen Künstler*innen offenzulegen, wie sie KI bei der Entstehung ihrer Musik eingesetzt haben. SongDNA gibt Hörer*innen zusätzlichen Kontext zu Künstler*innen und weiteren Mitwirkenden hinter einem Track. Die Künstler*innendetails zeigen Informationen auf Basis von Spotify Daten, darunter Karrieremeilensteine, Veröffentlichungshistorie und Tour-Aktivitäten. Der Schutz des Künstler*innen-Profils ermöglicht Künstler*innen, für Spotify angelieferte Veröffentlichungen zu prüfen und freizugeben. So lässt sich die eigene Künstler*innen-Identität besser schützen und Verwechslungen durch falsch zugeordnete Musik können vermieden werden. Zusätzlich zu diesen Funktionen stimmen wir unsere Algorithmen darauf ab, authentische menschliche Künstler*innen hervorzuheben. Auf Basis der verfügbaren Signale arbeiten wir außerdem daran, Spam und minderwertige Inhalte aus unseren Empfehlungen herauszuhalten. Wir wissen, dass sich das Musik-Ökosystem weiterentwickelt, und unser Ansatz wird sich mit ihm verändern. Wir werden uns auch künftig an neue Entwicklungen anpassen und aus dem Austausch mit Künstler*innen, Hörer*innen und Partner*innen aus der Musikindustrie lernen.

title: PIM vs PXM: What's the Difference and Which Do You Need?
summary: PIM stores and manages product data. PXM manages the full product experience built on that data. See the differences, a comparison table, and when you need which.
body_text: PIM (Product Information Management) and PXM (Product Experience Management) get used interchangeably, but they describe different scopes. A PIM stores, organizes, and governs your product data in one place. A PXM covers that and everything built on top of it: the content, images, translations, and channel-specific experiences your customers actually see. If you're evaluating platforms, the distinction matters because it determines what you'll still have to stitch together after you buy. What is a PIM? Product Information Management (PIM) software is the system of record for product data. It centralizes attributes, specifications, categories, digital assets, and relationships for every SKU, so that teams and channels all pull from one governed source instead of scattered spreadsheets and supplier feeds. A PIM answers the question: is our product data complete, accurate, and consistent? Typical PIM jobs: Centralize product data from suppliers, ERPs, and spreadsheets Standardize attributes and enforce a taxonomy Manage data quality, completeness, and approvals Feed accurate data to every sales channel What is a PXM? Product Experience Management (PXM) starts where the PIM's job ends. It takes governed product data and turns it into the experience a shopper meets: enriched attributes, on-brand descriptions, optimized images, localized content, and listings tailored to each channel's requirements. A PXM answers the question: does every customer, on every channel, meet product content that's complete, on-brand, and built to convert? Typical PXM jobs: Enrich missing or thin product data at scale Generate and govern product content (descriptions, titles, bullets) Adapt images and copy per channel and market Localize content for new regions Optimize listings for search engines and AI search PIM vs PXM: side-by-side PIM PXM Core job Store and govern product data Manage the full product experience built on that data Scope Data accuracy and consistency Data plus content, images, localization, and channel optimization Primary users Product data and catalog teams Data teams plus ecommerce, content, and marketing teams Output A clean, governed product record Channel-ready product experiences Question it answers Is our data right? Does our product content convert, everywhere it appears? Do you need a PIM or a PXM? You need at least a PIM if product data lives in spreadsheets, differs between channels, or takes days of manual work to prepare for launch. You need a PXM if clean data alone isn't the bottleneck: your team spends its time writing descriptions, fixing images, adapting content per marketplace, or localizing for new markets. That work sits outside a traditional PIM, which is why teams that own it end up buying a PIM plus several point tools. The practical answer for most growing catalogs is that the split is disappearing. A modern PXM includes the PIM layer rather than replacing it. Hypotenuse AI is built this way: an AI-native PIM at the core, with enrichment, content generation, image editing, and localization running on top of it in one governed workflow, so product data goes from raw to channel-ready without leaving the system. That's the PXM platform approach. Frequently asked questions Can a PXM replace a PIM? A PXM that includes a PIM layer can. If the PXM only layers content tools over a separate data store, you still need the PIM underneath. Check whether product data actually lives and gets governed inside the platform. Is PXM just a rebranded PIM? No. The PIM handles data management; PXM adds the content, image, localization, and channel work built on that data. The label matters less than the scope: look at whether the platform covers what your team actually spends time on. Where do CMS and DAM fit? A CMS manages your website content, a DAM manages your digital assets, and a PIM manages product data. See our full comparison: PIM vs CMS vs DAM . Conclusion PIM keeps your product data right. PXM makes that data work everywhere your products appear. If your bottleneck is data chaos, start with the PIM question. If your bottleneck is everything after the data, evaluate platforms on the full experience layer, and prefer ones where the PIM is built in rather than bolted on.

title: Dynamic Model Routing & Open Models in Snowflake Cortex AI
summary: Snowflake introduces dynamic model routing and expands open model access in Cortex AI to help organizations improve AI efficiency, performance, and cost.
body_text: AI investment is accelerating, but business value is not always keeping pace. As organizations deploy more agents and AI applications, using the most powerful model for every request can increase costs without meaningfully improving outcomes. The real question is not which model is best. It is which model is best suited to each task and how to choose one at scale. Snowflake is helping organizations achieve this balance with two new capabilities in Snowflake Cortex AI. Dynamic model routing (PrPr soon) through Cortex AI Gateway provides a unified foundation for governing agent connections, intelligently directing requests and optimizing AI consumption. Snowflake is also expanding its portfolio of open models, including DeepSeek-V4-Flash (PrPr) and GLM-5.3 (coming soon), giving organizations greater flexibility to match each workload with the right model. Better AI economics starts with the right model for the right task The economics of AI improve when organizations stop paying for more intelligence than a task requires. Snowflake calls this intelligence efficiency: the ability to turn compute, models, data and context into measurable business value. The goal is to match every task with the model that can deliver the required quality at the lowest appropriate cost, rather than defaulting every request to the most expensive option. The principle is simple: Not every task requires the most powerful model available. Generating a weekly status summary does not demand the same level of intelligence as synthesizing risk across an entire portfolio. The challenge is determining which model is best suited to each task and maintaining that mapping as dozens of models continue to evolve and improve. Introducing dynamic model routing in Cortex AI Gateway With dynamic model routing, Cortex AI Gateway selects the most affordable model that can confidently complete the task at each step of agent execution. Lower-complexity and repetitive tasks can be directed to more efficient models, while workloads that require deeper reasoning can be routed to frontier models. This helps customers reduce unnecessary inference spend without requiring development teams to build and maintain model-selection logic. As model choices, capabilities and pricing evolve, routing decisions can adapt without customers having to rebuild their applications or agents. The capability operates within the enterprise governance controls already established in Snowflake. It considers only administrator-approved models and respects an organization’s existing data residency settings, helping ensure that requests remain within approved compliance boundaries. Each routing decision is also logged, giving administrators and compliance teams visibility into which model handled which request. Early testing has demonstrated meaningful efficiency gains. In one internal evaluation, dynamic model routing completed a data build tool (dbt) pipeline workload with up to three times greater token efficiency than a frontier-model-only approach, while delivering comparable quality. In a separate coding-workload test, engineering teams maintained the same pull-request throughput while using approximately 25% fewer tokens.1 Because Snowflake maintains the routing layer, model selection can evolve as new models become available and the relative strengths of existing models change. Customers benefit from continuously improving routing without having to redesign their applications or manage complex routing logic themselves. Expanding open model access: DeepSeek-V4-Flash 0731 and GLM-5.3 A router is only as good as the options available to it. Dynamic model routing lowers costs by directing each request to the least expensive model that still meets the required quality bar. As the pool of capable, efficient models grows, the economics improves. With each new model addition to the pool, customers gain better performance at a lower cost. That’s why the open model ecosystem matters even more today than it did just a few months ago. Today we are expanding customers’ access to leading open models, including DeepSeek-V4-Flash 0731 (in private preview) and GLM-5.3 (private preview coming soon, subject to change based on model availability3) in Snowflake Cortex AI. These join an existing portfolio that includes models from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, Mistral AI and Meta, giving users more options to find the right combination of quality, performance and cost for each workload. Evaluated on ADE-bench using Snowflake CoCo as the agent harness, DeepSeek-V4-Flash scores 74.4%,2 outperforming the leading proprietary model we tested. That's not a rounding error; it's a signal that the OSS frontier has caught up where it matters most for data teams. While we’re announcing GLM 5.3 today, the GLM-5.2 scores from past tests tell a compelling story: solid data engineering accuracy (66% on ADE-bench2) with the lowest token footprint of any model in the benchmark, making it a strong fit for teams running high-volume, self-hosted workloads where cost and latency matter. DeepSeek-V4-Flash 0731 is available in CoCo today in private preview and GLM-5.3 is coming soon, self-hostable and designed to keep your data in your environment. Snowflake serves these open models itself rather than proxying a third-party API to ensure inference takes places within a secure perimeter. We operate the full path from raw enterprise data to a completed agentic task: the data, the compute running inference, the model weights and the agent harness orchestrating all of it. Several benefits follow directly from that: Inference runs next to governed data, reducing transfer cost and latency. Controlling the stack lets us optimize for the access patterns enterprise workloads actually produce, rather than accepting what a general-purpose endpoint delivers. Your data stays withinSnowflake’s governance boundary, so open models operate inside the same role-based access control and audit trail that already govern your data. AI economics that compound over time Together, dynamic model routing and a growing portfolio of open models can create compounding gains in intelligence efficiency. Dynamic routing reduces unnecessary reliance on costly frontier models by directing routine workloads to more efficient alternatives. At the same time, a broader selection of capable open models gives the routing layer more high-quality, cost-effective options for each request. The economics improve further as the system learns from real-world usage. As models are evaluated across different workloads, routing decisions become more precise. Tasks can be matched to the appropriate level of intelligence based on quality, latency, cost and governance requirements. As new models become available and existing models improve, a greater share of workloads can be handled by efficient models without compromising the outcomes the business requires. The result is a system that is designed to become more efficient over time by enabling organizations to progressively lower the average cost of each business outcome while continuing to benefit from advances in model performance. They can do so without rebuilding applications, hardcoding model choices or managing complex routing logic manually. Enterprise governance helps ensure that requests remain within defined compliance, performance and cost parameters, allowing organizations to scale AI with greater control and more sustainable economics. 1 Results based on Snowflake internal testing; methodology and conditions available upon request. Individual results may vary based on workload and configuration. 2 Efficiency score based on internal testing using ADE-bench, a framework created by dbt for evaluating AI agents on real-world analytics and data engineering tasks. 3 This content contains forward-looking statements, including about our future product offerings, and are not commitments to deliver any product offerings. Actual results and offerings may differ and are subject to known and unknown risk and uncertainties. See our latest 10-Q for more information.

title: AI Titans Unite at JFrog swampUP 2026 to Define the Future of the Software Supply Chain
summary: Software and security visionaries from Anthropic, Cursor, Google-Wiz, Microsoft, NVIDIA, and more unite at JFrog swampUP to chart the future of trusted software and AI delivery at scale
body_text: SUNNYVALE, Calif. – August 12, 2026 — JFrog Ltd (Nasdaq: FROG ), the Liquid Software company and creators of the JFrog Software Supply Chain Platform , the system of record for software artifacts, binaries, and AI assets, today announced the all-star speaker lineup for swampUP 2026 – the premier user conference for teams building, securing, and governing trusted software in the AI era – taking place September 1-3 at The Glasshouse in New York City. Register here. “Where else can you bring the leaders shaping AI together with the security and software experts delivering it at scale? That’s the power of JFrog swampUP,” said Shlomi Ben Haim, Co-Founder and CEO of JFrog. “As development shifts from human-paced to machine-generated, the software supply chain is being redefined, speed and trust can’t be compromised. We’re honored to welcome this extraordinary lineup of speakers and bring their vision together with the real-world best practices, experience, and innovation of our customers and community. Together, we’re here to shape what’s next.” Every enterprise is adding AI to their software supply chain, which is increasing the attack surface for bad actors. JFrog research shows attackers are no longer just breaching traditional defenses; they are actively weaponizing the trusted models, registries, and agentic tools fueling today’s AI-enabled development. Additionally, 97% of organizations claim AI governance while 53% are still pulling models from public registries where malicious payloads have been found. The gap between perceived security and operational reality has never been wider. The Leaders and Builders Driving the Next Era of AI & Security Innovation To help attendees navigate the rapidly shifting landscape of software supply chain security and governance in the agentic AI era, the 2026 swampUP speaker lineup brings together an extraordinary cross-section of security leaders, enterprise architects, and AI pioneers from the organizations defining what trusted, intelligent software delivery looks like in the AI era: Anthropic’s Jason Clinton, Deputy CISO , will bring a security leadership perspective to the growing risks and governance challenges created as AI reshapes how software is built and delivered. AT&T’s VP of Global Software & Product Delivery, Rinat Zilberstein , will join Shlomi Ben Haim, JFrog Co-Founder and CEO , to discuss how global enterprises must approach software supply chain security in the frontier AI era. Chainguard’s product leaders will join JFrog’s VP of AppSec, Eyal Dyment, to demonstrate how a self‑healing software supply chain, anchored on a single source of truth, enables automated, machine‑speed vulnerability detection and fixes in minutes. Cursor’s Field CISO, David Pan , and JFrog’s Co-Founder and CTO, Yoav Landman , will explain why having a system of record is essential to secure and govern every package, model, AI asset, and release at scale – regardless of tools or pipelines. Microsoft Software Global Black Belt, Daniel Meppiel , and JFrog’s Yonatan Arbel, will unveil strategies for securing the “Agent Software Supply Chain” – because when agents build your software, they need to be governed too. Moderne’s CEO, Jonathan Schneider , Echo Security CTO, Eylam Milner , CTO for Broadcom’s Tanzu Division, James Watters , and Chainguard’s Field CTO, Behn Williams , will join JFrog’s Chief Strategy Officer, Gal Marder, on stage to discuss where remediation is headed as frontier AI models outpace traditional security cycles. NVIDIA’s Developer Experience Leader, Krishna Nadiminti , will explore how to translate SBOM data into actionable risk signals and build trusted supply chains for AI agent skills. TEAM8’s Partner and CISO in Residence, Tim Brown , former CISO of SolarWinds , will join a fireside chat drawing on firsthand experience and learnings from one of history’s biggest software supply chain attacks to help attendees better understand threat models to help prevent the next AI-driven attack. Unmatched Value Add for swampUP Attendees swampUP 2026 pairs a world-class speaker lineup with hands-on experiences designed to deliver immediate, practical value for business, IT, and developer audiences through: New Product Introductions & JFrog Executive Keynotes: Shlomi Ben Haim, Co-Founder and CEO, Yoav Landman, Co-Founder and CTO, and other leaders from across JFrog’s DevOps, Security, AI/ML and DevGovOps business, will take the stage to provide key insights grounded in customer data, JFrog Security Research, and JFrog Platform usage on the “Agentic Software Supply Chain” surge. Hands-on Training with Certification: Training Day labs and masterclasses, led by industry experts and emphasizing real-world experience, equip attendees with practical skills across the JFrog Platform and the broader DevOps toolchain. Breakout Sessions for Every Experience Level: Multi-track sessions on AI/ML model management, agent governance and security, DevSecOps, and Cloud-Native architecture, designed for executives, engineers, security teams, and AI/ML practitioners alike. Community Gala & Networking: An unforgettable evening at the Intrepid Museum in New York City, offering uninterrupted time to connect with peers from across the global software community, featuring keynote speaker Carey Lohrenz , the first female F-14 Tomcat Fighter Pilot in the U.S. Navy, sharing hard-won lessons on leading through uncertainty and making critical decisions when the stakes are highest. Registration is now open , and the full agenda is available at https://swampup.jfrog.com/ . For more information on reasons to attend swampUP 2026 visit https://swampup.jfrog.com/jyt/ or follow JFrog on LinkedIn and X @jfrog. ### Like this Story? Share this on X: Join Anthropic, @Cursor_ai , @Microsoft , #wiz, @googlecloud , @chainguard_dev , @ATT , @nvidiaAIDev & more at #swampUP 2026, Sept 1–3 NYC. Register: https://swampup.jfrog.com #DevSecOps #AI #SoftwareSupplyChain #DevGovOps #security About JFrog JFrog Ltd. (Nasdaq: FROG), the creators of the unified DevOps, DevSecOps, DevGovOps and MLOps platform, is on a mission to create a world of software delivered without friction from development to production. Driven by a “Liquid Software” vision, the JFrog Platform is a software supply chain system of record that is designed to power organizations as they build, manage, and distribute secure software with speed and scale. Holistic security features help identify, protect, and remediate against threats and vulnerabilities. The universal, hybrid, multi-cloud JFrog Platform is available as both SaaS services across major cloud service providers and self-hosted. Millions of users and approximately 6,600 organizations worldwide, including a majority of the Fortune 100, depend on JFrog solutions to securely embrace digital transformation in the AI era. Learn more at https://jfrog.com or follow us on X @JFrog. title: Clari vs Outreach.io: A complete guide for 2026
summary: Compare Clari vs Outreach.io across forecasting, sales engagement, AI, reporting, pricing, strengths, weaknesses, and discover which platform fits your team.
body_text: Choosing between Clari vs Outreach.io often comes down to one question: do you need better forecasting or better sales execution? In an ideal scenario, sales first businesses require both, but either one of these goals can be achieved. Unless and until you are using another software, like Trellus.ai , which supplements the overall effect of outreach, conversions and pipeline acceleration, you aren’t going to get too far. Yet again, there is also another angle that deserves just as much attention. How productive are your reps when they are on the phone? Why is this question important, and how does it fit into the situation? Well, as it turns out, even though both software are pretty good at what they do, cold calls and live conversations make up for a huge gain in sales conversions. Neither Clari nor Outreach was built to maximize live conversations. Clari excels as a revenue intelligence platform, helping leadership understand pipeline health and forecast revenue. Outreach is one of the leading sales engagement platforms, helping teams automate outreach across multiple channels. Yet both leave room for improvement when it comes to helping reps have more productive conversations, make more quality dials, and convert those conversations into meetings. This is where Trellus.ai fits naturally into the modern sales stack. Rather than replacing your existing platform, it extends Outreach with an AI powered calling workspace built specifically for outbound sales teams. If Outreach manages your sequences and workflows, this platform helps your reps execute those sequences faster, smarter, and with far better coaching. Category Clari Outreach.io Primary Focus Revenue Intelligence Forecasting, pipeline visibility, RevOps analytics Sales Engagement Sequences, outreach automation, seller productivity Best For Enterprise revenue leaders, CROs, RevOps and Finance teams Outbound SDRs, AEs, Sales Managers and Revenue Teams Forecasting ★★★★★ Industry-leading AI forecasting with historical pipeline tracking ★★★★☆ Good forecasting built around sales activity Sales Engagement ★★☆☆☆ Basic engagement capabilities ★★★★★ Multi-channel engagement and sequencing Email Automation Limited Advanced sequence automation Call Management Conversation intelligence and activity tracking Integrated calling with AI coaching (Kaia) Conversation Intelligence Excellent AI insights from recorded calls Excellent live meeting assistance and coaching Pipeline Visibility Excellent executive-level visibility Strong opportunity-level visibility Reporting Executive dashboards and revenue analytics Sales activity, sequence, conversion and coaching reports CRM Sync Salesforce, HubSpot and enterprise CRMs Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, HubSpot and others AI Features Revenue forecasting, deal inspection, pipeline risk detection Kaia AI, sequence optimization, conversation insights and recommendations Implementation Complex Requires RevOps planning Moderate Requires sequence and workflow setup Learning Curve High Moderate to High Enterprise Scalability ★★★★★ ★★★★★ Pricing Custom enterprise pricing Custom enterprise pricing Biggest Strength Accurate forecasting and revenue intelligence Outbound automation and sales execution Main Limitation Not designed for outbound execution Forecasting not as comprehensive as Clari Ideal Buyer CRO, VP Revenue, RevOps Director VP Sales, SDR Manager, Outbound Teams Overall Verdict Choose Clari if forecasting and revenue visibility are your highest priorities. Choose Outreach if sales engagement, prospecting and outbound execution matter most. Why Many Outreach Teams Add Trellus.ai Outbound success depends on far more than sending emails or building sequences. Reps need to reach more prospects, stay focused during conversations, capture accurate notes, and improve every day without waiting for a manager to review recordings. The platform was designed around those day to day realities. Some of its most valuable capabilities include: AI Parallel Dialing that dramatically increases live conversations without forcing reps to spend hours listening to ringing phones. Real time AI coaching that provides live suggestions and objection handling during active calls. AI Practice Calls that allow new SDRs to rehearse difficult conversations before speaking with prospects. Automatic call summaries and CRM ready notes that eliminate tedious administrative work. AI research that prepares relevant prospect insights before every conversation. Advanced analytics that identify coaching opportunities across the entire sales team. LinkedIn Superhuman functionality that connects prospect research directly into the outbound workflow. Voicemail drop capabilities that save valuable selling time during high volume calling sessions. But we’ll talk about them later, in detail, as we dig deeper into the analysis. A Better Alternative for Teams That Prioritize Outbound Performance If your evaluation centers on Clari vs Outreach.io , the answer often depends on your primary objective. Choose Clari when executive forecasting, pipeline inspection, and sales forecasting software capabilities are your biggest priorities. Choose Outreach when you need enterprise grade sequencing and engagement automation. However, if your organization already relies on Outreach and wants to increase meetings booked without replacing existing workflows, adding a dedicated AI calling platform often delivers a much faster return on investment than migrating to another engagement solution. This combination gives sales leaders the best of both worlds. Outreach continues orchestrating emails, sequences, and multi channel engagement while Trellus helps every representative execute more productive conversations, improve call quality, and spend significantly more time selling. For many outbound organizations, that combination creates a far more complete revenue engine than relying on a single platform alone. Comprehensive Analytics & Reporting Analytics often becomes the deciding factor after a sales platform has been running for a few months. Automating outreach is valuable. Building accurate forecasts matters. None of it means much if leadership cannot clearly see what is happening across the pipeline, where opportunities are getting stuck, and why certain reps consistently outperform others. This is where both platforms bring considerable value, although they serve different audiences inside the organization. When people search "Clari vs Outreach.io pricing and features comparison", reporting is one area that deserves careful attention. Both products provide extensive dashboards, AI powered insights, and customizable reporting. The difference comes down to the questions each platform is designed to answer. Outreach concentrates on sales execution. Clari concentrates on revenue visibility. Both belong among today's leading revenue operations tools, but they serve different parts of the revenue organization. Outreach Analytics & Reporting Outreach treats analytics as an extension of the selling process. Rather than presenting static reports, it continuously analyzes sales activity across emails, calls, meetings, sequences, and pipeline progression to help managers improve execution while deals are still active. Sales leaders can monitor individual representatives, compare teams, identify coaching opportunities, and understand which activities are generating meaningful business outcomes. Since reports update continuously throughout the day, managers do not have to wait until weekly meetings to identify problems. The reporting environment includes dozens of prebuilt dashboards while also allowing organizations to build custom reports around their own KPIs, sales methodology, and operating model. Some of the areas Outreach tracks include: Sales activity metrics Pipeline progression Sequence performance Conversion rates Meeting outcomes Forecast trends Team productivity Outreach allows managers to drill down into the details. A manager might begin by noticing declining pipeline conversion, then move directly into specific sequences, individual calls, or rep activity to understand what caused the slowdown. This makes coaching considerably more focused. Rather than relying on assumptions, managers can point to measurable behaviors and help reps improve areas that directly impact revenue generation. Another advantage is the platform's close relationship with its conversation intelligence software capabilities. Calls, meetings, engagement activity, and CRM updates all contribute to a much richer reporting environment. Sales leaders gain visibility into both what happened and what happened during customer conversations. The result is a reporting environment built primarily for improving execution, helping frontline managers coach faster, identify winning behaviors, and keep sales teams moving toward quota. Clari Revenue Operations Analytics While Outreach looks closely at seller activity, Clari starts several levels higher. Its reporting environment is designed for executives, CROs, finance leaders, and RevOps teams responsible for understanding the health of the entire revenue organization. As a leading revenue intelligence platform, Clari brings together CRM data, historical pipeline changes, forecasting models, account health indicators, and revenue trends into one centralized reporting experience. Rather than asking, "How productive was this sales rep today?", Clari answers much broader business questions. Examples include: Is pipeline coverage sufficient for next quarter? Which regions are becoming forecast risks? Which managers consistently overcommit forecasts? Which products are producing higher win rates? How is average sales cycle changing over time? Which territories require additional investment? Where is revenue leakage beginning to appear? Its dashboards are designed around executive decision making rather than day to day sales activity. The platform tracks a wide range of strategic metrics, including: Pipeline coverage ratios. Stage conversion rates. Average deal value. Sales cycle duration. Win rates across products and territories. Forecast accuracy. One area where Clari continues to stand apart among sales forecasting software providers is historical data preservation. Because its RevDB architecture captures every meaningful pipeline change over time , leadership can review historical movement across entire quarters rather than relying only on today's CRM snapshot. This provides valuable context during quarterly business reviews, board meetings, strategic planning sessions, and territory design exercises. Trend analysis also becomes considerably stronger because leadership can compare multiple quarters using consistent historical data instead of incomplete CRM records. For growing enterprise organizations, these reporting capabilities support: More confident revenue forecasting. Better quota planning. Improved territory design. Smarter resource allocation. Early identification of pipeline risk. For executive teams responsible for long term planning, these insights often become as valuable as forecasting itself. Clari vs Outreach.io: Which Reporting Experience Fits Your Team? When people ask, "What is the difference between Clari and Outreach.io?", analytics provides one of the clearest answers. Outreach builds reports around seller execution. Every dashboard helps managers understand how sales activities influence meetings, opportunities, and pipeline generation. It is an excellent choice for organizations looking to improve outbound performance, coaching effectiveness, and daily productivity. Clari approaches reporting from a revenue leadership perspective. Every dashboard is built to improve forecasting confidence, pipeline visibility, strategic planning, and executive decision making across the business. Neither reporting philosophy is universally better. Organizations investing heavily in outbound prospecting usually gain more immediate value from Outreach's execution focused reporting. Companies managing large enterprise revenue organizations often benefit more from Clari's broader revenue intelligence capabilities. For many enterprise sales teams, the answer to "Can Clari and Outreach.io be used together in a sales tech stack?" is yes. Outreach generates the sales activity, while Clari transforms that activity into executive level revenue insights. The combination creates a reporting ecosystem that supports both frontline sales management and long term revenue planning. Our Take Both products deliver excellent reporting capabilities, but they answer very different business questions. Outreach tells managers how their sales organization is performing today and where coaching can improve results. Clari tells leadership how the entire revenue engine is performing and how likely the business is to achieve future revenue targets. Your decision should come down to the problems you need your reporting platform to solve. If improving rep execution sits at the top of your priority list, Outreach offers one of the most comprehensive analytics environments available within a modern sales engagement platform. If executive visibility and forecasting accuracy carry greater weight, Clari continues to lead among enterprise revenue operations tools. Strengths & Weaknesses Every sales platform comes with tradeoffs. No product excels at everything, especially in enterprise sales where forecasting, prospecting, coaching, and revenue operations all require different capabilities. This is one of the biggest reasons the Clari vs Outreach.io discussion continues year after year. Both platforms are leaders in their respective categories, but they were built with different priorities in mind. Clari focuses on helping revenue leaders understand pipeline health and improve forecasting confidence . Outreach concentrates on helping sales teams engage more prospects, execute consistently, and close more opportunities. If you're researching "Best Clari and Outreach.io alternatives for revenue teams in 2026", understanding where each platform shines and where it falls short will make the decision much easier. Outreach Strengths Outreach has earned its reputation as one of the leading sales engagement platforms because it combines automation, AI, coaching, and workflow management into one ecosystem. Sales organizations looking to improve outbound execution often find that it replaces several smaller tools while giving managers much better visibility into team performance. AI Sales Engagement Sales engagement has evolved far beyond scheduled email sequences. Outreach uses artificial intelligence to help sales teams determine which prospects deserve immediate attention, which accounts are beginning to lose momentum, and which actions have the highest probability of moving opportunities forward. Rather than asking reps to manually prioritize hundreds of accounts every morning, the platform continuously evaluates engagement signals and recommends where sellers should spend their time. This reduces guesswork and helps teams focus their energy on conversations that are more likely to generate meetings and revenue. Real Time Coaching with Kaia One of Outreach's biggest strengths is Kaia, its AI powered coaching assistant. During live meetings and sales calls, Kaia listens to conversations, captures important discussion points, surfaces relevant information, and helps representatives remain focused throughout customer interactions. Managers also gain valuable coaching material after conversations end. Rather than reviewing hours of recordings manually, they can quickly identify objection handling patterns, missed opportunities, pricing discussions, and competitive mentions. For organizations investing heavily in conversation intelligence software , Kaia provides valuable support for onboarding, coaching, and ongoing sales development. Predictive Analytics & Forecasting Although forecasting is not Outreach's original foundation, the platform has invested heavily in predictive revenue capabilities. Its forecasting engine combines CRM activity, conversation data, engagement metrics, and opportunity progression to estimate future revenue outcomes. Sales leaders gain greater visibility into pipeline health while managers receive earlier warning signs when deals begin slowing down. Organizations that already rely heavily on Outreach for execution often appreciate having forecasting available inside the same environment rather than purchasing another standalone solution. Opportunity Management Complex enterprise opportunities involve multiple buyers, lengthy buying cycles, and dozens of customer interactions. Outreach provides a centralized workspace where representatives can organize activities, monitor stakeholder engagement, manage follow ups, and keep opportunities progressing through every sales stage. Rather than forcing reps to switch between several applications throughout the day, much of their daily workflow remains inside one interface. This helps improve consistency while reducing administrative overhead. Comprehensive Analytics & Reporting Reporting remains another major advantage. Sales leaders gain continuous visibility into team activity, conversion rates, sequence performance, pipeline progression, and coaching opportunities. Managers can move from executive dashboards into detailed rep activity within seconds, making coaching conversations much more evidence based than opinion driven. For organizations managing large outbound teams, this reporting environment becomes an important operational tool rather than simply a collection of dashboards. Outreach Weaknesses No platform is perfect, and Outreach comes with a learning curve that prospective buyers should understand before making an investment. Advanced Features Require Time to Master Outreach offers an enormous number of capabilities. While this creates tremendous value for mature sales organizations, it also means administrators need time to configure sequences, permissions, reporting structures, automation rules, and AI workflows correctly. Teams expecting a plug and play experience may underestimate the amount of planning required before realizing the platform's full potential. International Data Quality Can Vary Organizations selling globally should carefully evaluate data coverage across their target markets. Certain regions have richer contact information than others, which can influence prospecting efficiency depending on where your sales team operates. Running pilot campaigns across your primary markets remains a smart step before committing to a large rollout. AI Still Benefits from Human Oversight Artificial intelligence continues improving every year, but sales conversations still require human judgment. AI generated emails, summaries, recommendations, and insights should always receive a quick review before reaching customers. This helps maintain brand voice, improve personalization, and avoid small errors that can reduce credibility during important customer interactions. Clari Strengths Clari has established itself as one of the leading revenue intelligence platforms because every feature revolves around helping revenue organizations improve forecasting confidence and pipeline visibility. Large enterprise businesses often choose Clari because executive leadership requires accurate answers long before quarter end. Revenue Forecasting AI Forecasting remains Clari's biggest competitive advantage . The platform analyzes historical CRM changes, opportunity movement, sales activity, pipeline trends, and deal progression to generate highly accurate revenue forecasts. Its RevDB architecture preserves historical pipeline movement over time, giving forecasting models much richer context than standard CRM reporting alone. For organizations evaluating Clari vs Outreach.io: which platform is better for sales forecasting?, this remains one of Clari's clearest strengths. Pipeline Inspection & Deal Health Sales managers spend countless hours reviewing opportunities that may never close. Clari simplifies this process through automated deal health analysis, highlighting opportunities showing warning signs before they become forecast surprises. Managers can quickly identify declining engagement, stalled opportunities, missing customer interactions, and other indicators that deserve immediate attention. This allows coaching conversations to focus on the highest risk opportunities rather than reviewing every deal individually. Conversation Intelligence Clari also includes robust conversation intelligence software capabilities through its acquisition strategy. Sales calls are automatically recorded, transcribed, and analyzed for important customer insights, competitive mentions, objections, buying signals, and coaching opportunities. Revenue leaders gain a much deeper understanding of customer conversations without spending hours reviewing recordings manually. Activity Capture & Engagement Scoring Manual CRM updates remain one of the biggest frustrations for sales teams. Clari automatically captures emails, meetings, calendar events, and customer interactions, helping organizations maintain cleaner CRM records while reducing administrative work for representatives. Engagement scoring also provides leadership with greater visibility into account health across the pipeline. Revenue Operations Analytics Beyond forecasting, Clari delivers extensive reporting designed specifically for executives and RevOps professionals. Leadership can monitor pipeline coverage, territory performance, forecast accuracy, revenue trends, sales cycle movement, and historical business performance from one centralized environment. These capabilities make Clari particularly valuable for organizations managing large enterprise revenue operations. Clari Weaknesses Although Clari leads the market in several areas, prospective buyers should understand its limitations before making a long term investment. Enterprise Deployment Requires Planning Clari offers deep functionality across forecasting, reporting, AI analysis, and revenue operations. Configuring these capabilities to match complex enterprise sales processes often requires experienced RevOps resources and careful implementation planning. Organizations with smaller sales teams may not require this level of sophistication. Platform Value Depends on CRM Quality Like every sales forecasting software solution, Clari depends heavily on the quality of CRM data. Missing activities, outdated contacts, inaccurate opportunity stages, and inconsistent pipeline management reduce forecasting accuracy regardless of how advanced the AI models become. Clean CRM processes remain essential for achieving the best results. AI Recommendations Still Need Human Judgment Clari surfaces valuable insights, predicts forecast outcomes, and identifies revenue risks, but final business decisions still belong to experienced sales leaders. Forecasts should support leadership discussions, not replace them. The strongest organizations combine AI recommendations with frontline manager knowledge and executive experience before making strategic decisions. Wrapping It Up… Comparing strengths and weaknesses makes one point very clear. Outreach excels when your priority is helping sales teams execute better, engage more prospects, and improve daily selling activities through one comprehensive sales engagement platform. Clari excels when leadership needs dependable forecasting, executive visibility, and enterprise grade revenue operations tools that provide confidence in every revenue discussion. For many organizations, these platforms solve complementary problems rather than competing head to head. Understanding your biggest operational priority remains the simplest way to decide which solution deserves a place in your sales technology stack.

title: Ferrovial selected to deliver Tennessee’s I-24 Choice Lanes
summary: Ferrovial, a leading global infrastructure company, today announced it has been selected to deliver Tennessee’s I-24 Southeast Choice Lanes in Nashville, the largest single capital investment and first public-private partnership in Tennessee’s history.
body_text: Ferrovial , a leading global infrastructure company, today announced it has been selected to deliver Tennessee’s I-24 Southeast Choice Lanes in Nashville, the largest single capital investment and first public-private partnership in Tennessee’s history. “We are honored to be selected to deliver this landmark transportation project for Tennessee, which will enhance mobility and support the state’s continued economic success, ” said Ignacio Madridejos, Ferrovial CEO. “As communities across the U.S. continue to grow, innovative infrastructure investment is essential to meeting future transportation needs . We look forward to delivering a project that improves connectivity and creates value for decades to come.” The 26-mile project will add choice lanes in both directions along I-24 between Nashville and Murfreesboro, improving mobility along one of the region’s most congested corridors . The Ferrovial-led consortium, DriveTN, which includes Transurban and Tikehau Star Infra, will finance, design, build, operate and maintain the $9.2 billion project, while providing a projected $24.8 billion in concession value to Tennessee. The I-24 Southeast Choice Lanes project will provide a cost-effective transportation solution offering reliable travel times along a key corridor extending from I-40 east of downtown Nashville to I-840 near Murfreesboro. Drivers who choose to use the lanes will benefit from more consistent travel speeds, even during peak periods, while those remaining in the free general-purpose lanes will also experience reduced congestion. Ferrovial has successfully replicated this model in other growing U.S. metropolitan areas, including Dallas-Fort Worth, Charlotte and Washington, D.C. On Virginia’s 66 Express Outside the Beltway corridor, similar express lanes have reduced peak travel times by as much as 50 percent while providing reliable trip conditions. By bringing that experience to Tennessee, the project will deliver lasting mobility benefits and support continued growth across the region . * This press release includes inside information in accordance with article 7 of the Market Abuse Regulation

title: enCore Energy Reports Q2 2026 Financial Results
summary: Browse enCore Energy Corp. news releases and announcements about U.S. ISR uranium production and corporate developments.
body_text: DALLAS , Aug. 13, 2026 /CNW/ — enCore Energy Corp. (NASDAQ: EU) (TSXV: EU) (the " Company " or " enCore "), America's Clean Energy CompanyTM, announced today its financial and operational results for the six months ended June 30, 2026. Results for the six months ended June 30, 2026 include: Loss per Share: Net loss per share of $0.19 versus $0.16 for the same period 2025. The increased loss was driven primarily by lower extraction and a fair value adjustment of Verdera Energy Corp. shares, as described in the Form 10-Q; Uranium Deliveries: Delivery into contracts of 485,000 pounds of uranium ("U3O8") at an average sales price of $70.10 per pound, compared to 350,000 pounds of U3O8 at an average sales price of $62.58 per pound in the same period 2025; Operating Margin: Weighted average cost of delivered U3O8 increased to $75.54 per pound including 360,000 purchased pounds, compared to a weighted average cost of $59.42 per pound in the same period 2025; Uranium Extraction: U3O8 extraction of 131,274 pounds, a decrease from 317,613 pounds during the same period 2025; Costs: Higher year to date 2026 extraction costs of $57.36 per pound compared to $42.92 for the same period 2025 due to lower extraction; Inventory: Closing balance of 203,304 pounds of U3O8 in inventory at a weighted average cost of $70.81 per pound; Total liquidity of $88.4 million, including $21.8 million of unrestricted cash, $52.2 million of marketable securities, and $14.4 million of inventory. Adjusted total liquidity as of June 30, 2026 was $73.5 million, which excludes marketable securities of $14.9 million in Verdera Energy Corp. Operational Updates: Alta Mesa Project: Final permitting to begin extraction operations from Wellfield 3 Extension is anticipated in Q4-2026. Costs have been fully expensed, and the Wellfield is ready for immediate operation upon receipt of final permits. Alta Mesa's Wellfield 7 is scheduled to cease recovery during Q3-2026 due to anticipated depletion as the end of its natural life approaches. Final permits for Wellfield 8 are anticipated by the end of Q1-2027; Alta Mesa East Exploration: Drilling with 3 to 5 rigs continued throughout the quarter and is ongoing. Results to date have met or exceeded expectations and initial permitting is underway. Drilling is projected to continue through the current quarter and into Q4-2026. New drill results will be reported in the coming weeks and months; Rosita Project and Upper Spring Creek Project: Initial start-up extraction from the Upper Spring Creek Wellfield and Satellite IX Plant is anticipated to feed the Rosita Central Processing Plant immediately upon receipt of final permits, which are anticipated in Q4-2026. Costs have been fully expensed in prior periods and the plant is ready for immediate operation upon receipt of final permits; Improved Outlook: The new operation at Upper Spring Creek coupled with the new wellfields at Alta Mesa position enCore for improved extraction and greater operating efficiency as the Company moves into 2027; Dewey Burdock ISR Uranium Project: On June 22, 2026, the Company announced important permitting progress highlighted by the Dewey Burdock ISR Uranium Project receiving a 20-year renewal of the Source Materials License (SUA-1600) effective until June 2046, following the Bureau of Land Management approval to commence infrastructure construction. The Project has now received all necessary federal permits. The Project entered State of South Dakota permitting on June 15, 2026, which is under review by the Department of Agriculture & Natural Resources. Although we anticipate development in 2028, this is subject to receiving permits from the state; Reduction in Expenses: In July 2026, management executed on its plan for reducing costs with a reduction in workforce following a rationalization of staffing needs across the Company. While this reduction was initiated during the second quarter, the significant savings realized from this action will not be realized until the third quarter financials and beyond. The Company remains focused on disciplined execution, strengthening its balance sheet and improving its uranium extraction to meet growing U.S. utility demand. Additional Updates On August 17, 2026, the Company will award equity grants under its 2024 Long-Term Incentive Plan (the "Plan") to certain of its directors and officers. These grants consist of (i) 351,350 restricted stock units ("RSUs") that vest one (1) year from the grant date; (ii) 409,189 RSUs that vest ratably over three (3) years from the grant date; (iii) 461,757 performance stock units that vest based on the achievement of applicable performance goals at the conclusion of the three-year period ending December 31, 2028; and (iv) 101,351 stock options that vest ratably over three (3) years from the grant date with an exercise price equal to the closing price of the Company's common shares on the grant date and expiring five (5) years after the grant date, all of which are subject to the terms and conditions of the Plan. Investor Information enCore's interim financial statements, including the accompanying Management's Discussion and Analysis, are available in the Company's Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q, which is being filed today with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC") and with Canadian securities regulators on SEDAR+. It includes the Company's consolidated financial statements for the six months ended June 30, 2026, and the related notes and financial results. The report can be accessed at SEC's website at www.sec.gov , SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca , and on enCore's financials page at www.encoreuranium.com/investors/financial-statements/ . About enCore Energy Corp. enCore Energy Corp., America's Clean Energy Company™, is committed to providing clean, reliable, and affordable uranium to fuel the rapidly expanding U.S. nuclear energy needs. enCore's team is led by industry experts with extensive knowledge and experience in all aspects of uranium ISR operations and the nuclear fuel cycle. enCore exclusively uses ISR for uranium extraction, a minimally invasive, eco-friendly, and economically competitive mineral extraction technology co-developed by enCore's leadership. Building on enCore's demonstrated and continuing success in South Texas, future projects in enCore's planned project pipeline include the expansion of Alta Mesa to include the Alta Mesa East property, the Dewey Burdock project in South Dakota, and the Gas Hills project in Wyoming. title: Managing Complex Tax Filings for a Chemical Company
summary: See how CBIZ navigated complex multi-state tax filings for a chemical company, ensuring accurate K-1 updates and compliance across 40 states.
body_text: Issue The client’s situation became particularly challenging due to a last-minute ownership change that occurred after a partner’s passing. This event happened after the state K-1s had already been distributed to all the partners, adding an extra layer of complexity to the process. Solution The main obstacle was to update only the affected partners’ K-1s across about 40 states, while ensuring that the other partners’ information remained unchanged. This task was complicated by limitations within our tax preparation systems, as well as federal overrides that did not flow cleanly to the state-level returns. CBIZ had multiple discussions with the team and closely reviewed the changes they implemented. We provided guidance and feedback to uphold the accuracy in state filings and special income allocations setup. Our regular check-ins and open communication channels enabled the team to solve problems collectively and adapt appropriate strategies as needed. Outcome As a result of comprehensive team guidance and effective project leadership, we achieved successful and accurate filings that met all compliance requirements and exceeded the client’s expectations.
