title: Getting Started with npm Workspaces
summary: npm workspaces setup, commands, and limits: manage a monorepo, link sibling packages, and know when to add Turborepo or Nx.
body_text: npm workspaces, built into npm since version 7, let you manage several packages in one repository — a monorepo — from a single root: one npm install hoists shared dependencies into a single root node_modules and symlinks your own packages there, so cross-package imports resolve with no npm link and no republishing. If you have an app plus a shared library, or a component library plus its docs site, and you’re tired of npm link , copy-pasting code, or juggling separate repos, this is the built-in feature that removes that friction — no third-party tool required. This guide covers the minimal config, the exact command flags, the real limitations, and when to layer a build orchestrator on top. Key Takeaways npm workspaces ship with npm 7+; the current release is npm 11.18.0 , and you can confirm your version with npm -v . The minimal setup is two files: a root package.json with "private": true and "workspaces": ["packages/*"] , plus one package.json per package — then a single npm install at the root wires everything together. To depend on a sibling package, add it by name with a "*" range; npm symlinks it on install, so edits to the source are visible in every consumer immediately, with no rebuild or republish. npm workspaces resolves and links dependencies but does not run tasks in dependency order, cache build outputs, or compute an “affected” graph. Reach for Turborepo or Nx on top of npm workspaces, not instead of it — npm resolves and links packages; those tools add task orchestration and caching. How do npm workspaces work? npm workspaces turn a single repository into a monorepo by hoisting shared dependencies into one root node_modules and symlinking your own packages alongside them. When you run npm install at the root, npm scans every workspace, installs third-party dependencies once at the top level, and links each local package into node_modules by its name field. If two of your packages depend on each other, the reference resolves through that symlink — the npm CLI automates the linking as part of npm install and removes the need to manually run npm link . The same workspaces field and symlink model also power Yarn, pnpm, and Bun, so the mental model transfers across package managers. The feature landed in npm 7; anything newer works. What is the minimal npm workspaces setup? The minimal setup is two files: a root package.json that declares where packages live, plus one package.json per package. Create this structure: my-monorepo/ ├── package.json # root — private, lists workspaces └── packages/ ├── utils/ │ └── package.json # @myorg/utils └── app/ └── package.json # @myorg/app The root package.json needs two fields: { " name " : " my-monorepo " , " private " : true , " workspaces " : [ " packages/* " ] } "private": true prevents you from accidentally publishing the root, and the packages/* glob tells npm to treat every directory under packages/ as a workspace. Give each package a scoped name like @myorg/utils to avoid registry collisions: { " name " : " @myorg/utils " , " version " : " 1.0.0 " , " main " : " dist/index.js " } Run npm install once at the root . There is a single lockfile at the root and no node_modules inside individual packages — everything hoists up. Add a cross-package dependency To depend on a sibling package, add it by name with a "*" range; npm symlinks it on install, so edits to the source are visible in every consumer immediately. In @myorg/app : { " name " : " @myorg/app " , " dependencies " : { " @myorg/utils " : " * " } } Run npm install at the root again. npm creates a symlink from node_modules/@myorg/utils to packages/utils , and you import it like any published module: import { formatDate } from " @myorg/utils " ; Because it’s a symlink, changing the source in packages/utils is reflected in app with no rebuild or republish — this is the payoff over npm link . One cross-tool caveat: npm does not support the workspace: version protocol that pnpm and Yarn Berry use. Passing a workspace: specifier makes npm fail with EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL , so with npm you reference internal packages by name and range ( "*" ), not workspace:* . The daily commands The flags trip people up because singular and plural mean different things. Add a dependency to one package with -w , to every package with --workspaces ; run a script in one workspace with -w , and across all of them with --workspaces --if-present , which skips packages that don’t define that script. # Install a dep into ONE workspace npm install lodash -w @myorg/app # Install a dev dep into one workspace npm install -D vitest -w @myorg/utils # Install a dep into EVERY workspace npm install eslint --workspaces # Run a script in ONE workspace npm run build -w @myorg/utils # Run a script across ALL workspaces, skipping those without it npm run test --workspaces --if-present -w is shorthand for --workspace , and --workspaces (or -ws ) targets all of them. Wire the root scripts once so npm run build fans out: { " scripts " : { " build " : " npm run build --workspaces --if-present " , " test " : " npm run test --workspaces --if-present " } } To verify the graph is linked, run npm ls -ws or query it with npm query .workspace . The limits: what npm workspaces won’t do npm workspaces resolves and links dependencies, but it does not run tasks in dependency order, cache build outputs, or compute an “affected” graph. If your app imports a library, you must build the library first — running a script across workspaces will error when they depend on each other because npm does not execute in topological order , an enhancement that remains open. Order it explicitly, or use npm-run-all : { " scripts " : { " build:utils " : " npm run build -w @myorg/utils " , " build:app " : " npm run build -w @myorg/app " , " build " : " npm run build:utils && npm run build:app " } } Two more gotchas: Nested node_modules . When two packages require incompatible versions of the same dependency, npm stops hoisting and installs a nested copy inside one package. Pin a single shared version with the root overrides field to keep the tree flat: { " overrides " : { " lodash " : " ^4.17.21 " } } Install-script defaults are tightening. npm v12, estimated to release in July 2026 , changes allowScripts to default off, so npm install will no longer run dependency preinstall , install , or postinstall scripts unless explicitly allowed. If your workspaces rely on a postinstall or prepare build step, plan to approve it — these changes surface as warnings on npm 11.16.0 or newer so you can prepare early. Note that “no native React/Vue/Vite integration” is a scope statement, not a defect: workspaces are framework-agnostic by design. Scaffolding apps is not their job. When to reach for Turborepo or Nx Reach for Turborepo or Nx on top of npm workspaces, not instead of it: npm resolves and links your packages, while those tools add task orchestration, caching, and affected-graph builds for larger repos. They’re complementary layers. Concern npm workspaces Turborepo / Nx Install & link packages ✅ Delegates to npm Task dependency order ❌ manual scripts ✅ topological Build/test caching ❌ ✅ local + remote ”Affected” builds ❌ ✅ change-based graph Add one when ordered scripts get unwieldy, CI rebuilds everything on every change, or you want to run tasks only for packages a commit touched. Note that modern Lerna is now Nx-backed — the old “npm + Lerna” advice has folded into this same layering. npm workspaces covers roughly the first 80% of small-monorepo needs with zero extra tooling. Scaffold the two-file config, wire your flags, order your builds, and add an orchestrator only when the pipeline — not the dependency resolution — becomes the bottleneck. Run on an Active LTS Node release (Node 20 reached end-of-life on 2026-04-30) and confirm npm -v reports 7 or newer before you start. FAQs Does npm workspaces still need one lockfile per package, or one at the root? npm workspaces produces a single package-lock.json at the repository root, not one per package. A root npm install resolves every workspace's dependencies together and records them in that one lockfile, while individual packages get no node_modules directory of their own because dependencies hoist to the root. This single-lockfile model is what keeps versions consistent across all packages and is why you always run install from the root. Why does 'npm run build --workspaces' fail when my packages depend on each other? It fails because npm does not run workspace scripts in topological (dependency) order; it runs them in the order workspaces are listed, so a consumer can build before the library it imports exists, producing 'cannot find module' or failed-resolve errors. This remains an open npm enhancement (issue 4139). Fix it by defining explicit ordered scripts that build the library first, or by using a tool like npm-run-all, Turborepo, or Nx. Can I use the 'workspace:*' protocol with npm like I do in pnpm or Yarn? No. npm does not support the workspace: version protocol used by pnpm and Yarn Berry, and passing a workspace: specifier makes npm fail with EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL (documented in npm/cli issue 8845). With npm, reference internal packages by their name and a normal range such as '@myorg/utils': '*'; npm symlinks them on install. If you migrate a pnpm or Yarn repo to npm, rewrite every workspace: specifier to a plain range. Do I still need 'npm link' when using workspaces? No. npm workspaces automate linking as part of npm install, symlinking each local package into the root node_modules by its name field, which removes the need to manually run npm link. Once a package lists a sibling as a dependency with a '*' range, a single root npm install wires the symlink, and edits to the source package are visible in every consumer immediately with no rebuild or republish. summary: Avaliar uma experiência de Odontologia no exterior exige separar duas perguntas que costumam se misturar: onde e como estudar. Entenda!
body_text: Perguntas frequentes Preciso fazer intercâmbio para ter alguma experiência internacional em Odontologia? Não. O intercâmbio é apenas uma das modalidades possíveis. Também é possível buscar estágios, pesquisas acadêmicas, especializações pontuais ou, em outro extremo, uma graduação completa no exterior, dependendo do momento acadêmico e do objetivo de cada estudante. Estudar Odontologia no exterior garante que poderei atuar como dentista naquele país? Não. Estudar em outro país e obter autorização para exercer a profissão são processos distintos. Para atuar como dentista no exterior, é necessário validar o diploma e se registrar no órgão profissional do país, seguindo regras específicas que devem ser confirmadas diretamente com esse órgão. O que é mobilidade acadêmica em Odontologia? É um período, geralmente de um semestre, em que o estudante cursa disciplinas em uma instituição parceira no exterior mantendo o vínculo com a universidade de origem no Brasil. É diferente de uma graduação completa cursada fora do país. Como funciona a bolsa de especialização em Implantodontia oferecida pelo ITI? A bolsa oferece formação em Implantodontia em centros de treinamento localizados em diferentes países, com financiamento custeado pela própria instituição e inscrições abertas até 15 de junho de 2026. Os detalhes de elegibilidade e seleção estão no edital oficial do programa. Harvard aceita alunos direto da graduação em Odontologia? Não. A Harvard School of Dental Medicine oferece apenas programas de pós-graduação e exige diploma de bacharel para ingresso, o que a torna inacessível para quem ainda não concluiu uma formação prévia. Quais fatores devo considerar ao escolher país e instituição para estudar Odontologia fora? Reputação e adequação ao seu momento acadêmico, idioma de ensino, custo de vida e mensalidades, existência de bolsas, currículo e estrutura prática oferecida, além da compatibilidade de créditos quando o objetivo é mobilidade acadêmica e não graduação completa. Que benefícios uma experiência internacional pode trazer para a formação em Odontologia? Um estudo sobre o programa Ciência sem Fronteiras identificou ganhos em independência, comunicação e pensamento crítico entre estudantes de Odontologia que participaram de intercâmbios, resultado do contato com outro contexto educacional e clínico. Aprofunde-se em: Odontologia no SUS: como é a carreira do dentista na saúde pública Planejando sua jornada internacional em Odontologia Avaliar uma experiência internacional em Odontologia exige separar duas perguntas que costumam se misturar: onde e como estudar, e onde será possível atuar depois. As modalidades disponíveis, graduação completa, mobilidade acadêmica, estágio, pesquisa ou especialização, atendem a objetivos diferentes, e a escolha entre elas deve considerar idioma, custo, currículo e o momento acadêmico do estudante, não apenas a reputação da instituição. Antes de qualquer decisão financeira ou de matrícula, o passo mais seguro é consultar diretamente os canais oficiais da instituição escolhida e, se o objetivo envolver atuação profissional no exterior, também o órgão de classe do país de destino, já que a formação e a autorização para exercer a profissão seguem caminhos separados. A Quero Bolsa , uma plataforma que oferece bolsas de estudo de até 80% em mais de 1.000 instituições de ensino de todo o Brasil, pode ajudar você com isso! Os descontos estão disponíveis em vários tipos de curso: cursos de graduação (incluindo tecnólogos) cursos de pós-graduação cursos t écnicos cursos de idiomas cursos livres cursos preparatórios para concursos públicos Ah! E outra coisa boa também é que dá para escolher a melhor modalidade que se adequa à sua realidade, porque ela oferece tanto cursos presenciais quanto cursos EaD . title: Reliability Engineering in the AI Era
summary: See why reliability engineering must span code, testing, telemetry, and incidents as AI agents erase the boundary between pre-production and production.
body_text: Engineering leaders have been claiming to “shift quality left” for years but production remains stubbornly stuck out of reach of software engineers. The realm of production remains mysterious with tools no one has access to and UIs that wouldn’t make sense to engineers anyway. I’ve noticed a small but growing trend of large enterprises hiring Reliability Engineers instead of Site Reliability Engineers. Dropping one word looks cosmetic but I think it points to a much bigger change. We’ve dispensed with proper testing and so reliability issues have shifted into production. Unfortunately, the velocity with which AI agents generate bugs requires a re-think of this process. 🎯 Key Takeaways AI agents make implementation skills more portable, but they make operational context more valuable. Software development will split into vendor, multi-harness, on-premises, and bespoke factory patterns. Reliability needs one feedback loop connecting code, tests, telemetry, incidents, and customer behavior. The word that disappeared Obviously the entire industry is not renaming SREs but I am noticing a trend towards this job title and it fits within the broader trend of software engineering becoming software manufacturing . Job titles are messy, and “Reliability Engineer” also means something very different in manufacturing. Before calling this a new idea, it is worth going back to Google’s original 2016 book, Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (PDF) . Its contents cover release engineering, testing for reliability, software engineering in SRE, and reliable product launches. The original remit already crossed the production boundary. The shorter title may be restoring some of the breadth that the practice lost along the way. But current software roles show a real pattern. Robinhood has advertised for a Software Engineer focused on Reliability , including pre-production, integration, and load testing in the remit. OpsMill describes a Product Reliability Engineer who turns customer incidents into regression tests, product changes, and safer defaults. PointOne calls its equivalent role full-stack engineering at the intersection of product, infrastructure, and customer impact . These are not renamed operations jobs. They connect what happens in production to what gets designed, built, and tested next. The missing word is the interesting part. “Site” suggests a place where reliability work happens. Modern reliability is a property of the entire delivery system. Shift left shifted blame For years, engineering leaders told teams to shift left. The entire goal was to find defects earlier when they are cheaper to fix. In many businesses, “test in prod” is a euphemism for “my customers are my testers.” The implementation was often less impressive. We moved a test stage earlier in the pipeline. We added a security scanner. We gave developers another checklist. Then we called the transformation complete but AI is pointing out that this was not true. The problem was a lack of context and the wide gulf between the skills that make an engineer good at building features and the skills that help debug production. Any senior engineer knows that debugging complex systems is a discipline all its own. QA knew how the product was supposed to behave but almost always lacked realistic production conditions. Developers knew the code but not every way customers used it. SREs had the telemetry and incident history, but usually received the change after it had crossed the release boundary. Every role had a different context. The organizational pressure has not disappeared and in fact it keeps increasing. In healthcare, PractiTest’s 2026 State of Testing report says 65.4% of teams reported increased workloads, while budget growth was just 11.5% and team downsizing reached 53.8%. “Everyone owns quality” sounds empowering until it becomes “nobody has the time.” AI flattens the wrong gap AI coding agents change this division of labor, but not because they make expertise irrelevant. In three field experiments covering 4,867 developers, Microsoft Research measured a 26.08% increase in completed tasks among developers with access to a coding assistant. Less-experienced developers saw greater adoption and productivity gains. That compresses part of the skills gap. An engineer does not need ten years of shell scripting to investigate logs, write a load-test harness, or modify a deployment manifest. Of course the best software engineers still distinguish themselves from AI tools and the same is true of SREs. But for most folks, the agent can handle much of the implementation. But implementation is not judgment and judgment requires context and experience. Anthropic analyzed roughly 400,000 Claude Code sessions and found that people made about 70% of planning decisions while Claude made about 80% of execution decisions . Users with domain expertise succeeded more often, recovered from errors more effectively, and got more useful work from each instruction. AI makes coding knowledge more portable. It does not make production knowledge optional. In fact, it rewards the person who can explain what normal looks like, which failure matters, and how to prove a change is safe. That is reliability engineering. It embeds quality into every stage of the software development cycle by breaking down organizational and knowledge barriers. Production belongs in the prompt A coding agent limited to a repository sees an incomplete system. It can read the handler but not the malformed payload that breaks it. It can edit a timeout but not see the latency distribution that made the timeout dangerous. It can generate a test without knowing which customer workflow deserves protection. Give the agent production context and the work changes. Logs help it investigate. Traces reveal dependencies. SLOs define acceptable behavior. Incident history exposes known failure modes. Real traffic supplies the inputs developers forgot to invent. Control theory gives us a useful model for what comes next. Its aim is to use feedback to “drive the system to a desired state”: measure the output, compare it with a reference, and use the difference to change the system. In software, observability gives us the sensor. Logs, metrics, traces, and traffic show us what happened. But a sensor is not a controller. And Observability is not hypothesis testing. flowchart LR P[Production behavior] --> O[Observe signals] O --> C[Compare to goal] C --> D{Within bounds?} D -- Yes --> P D -- No --> A[Act or approve] A --> V[Verify change] V --> P That is the intermediate step where much of the industry has been stuck. We observe a deviation, page a human, and open a ticket. Modern reliability needs to close the loop by comparing production behavior with a set point—an SLO, a correctness rule, or a customer outcome—and feeding the difference back into regression tests, traffic replay, release criteria, rollback decisions, and agent context. The action can be automated or human-approved; the important part is that the evidence travels back into engineering. Observability got us from blind to measured. Reliability engineering must get us from measured to controlled. The industry already collects much of this information. Capgemini’s World Quality Report 2025–26 found that 94% of organizations review production data. Nearly half struggle to turn those observations into quality improvements. That is not an observability problem. It is a feedback-loop problem. Generation outran verification The quality system matters more because code generation is no longer the limiting step. DORA found that a 25% increase in AI adoption was associated with a 3.4% improvement in perceived code quality, yet a 7.2% reduction in delivery stability . Faster reviews and better-looking code did not automatically produce safer releases. DORA’s likely explanation was larger changes moving through systems that were not built to verify them. Recent outages make the warning concrete. GitHub reported 10 incidents in April 2026 and nine more in May . GitHub also said traffic was growing rapidly, driven partly by AI-assisted and agentic workflows. The direct causes varied: schema migrations, shared databases, DNS, rate limiting, and capacity saturation. AI did not cause every outage. It increased the activity flowing through systems whose failure modes were already present. AWS’s October 2025 disruption offers the same lesson without an AI connection. A latent race condition in automated DynamoDB DNS management cascaded into EC2, load balancing, Lambda, containers, authentication, and other services. Automation increased scale. It also increased the blast radius of an assumption that turned out to be wrong. We cannot build a software factory on top of a quality process designed for artisanal code volume. The factories are coming “Software factory” is quickly becoming more than a metaphor. The coding-agent vendors are moving up the stack from generating code to managing the environment around it: planning, execution, permissions, review, deployment, and monitoring. Anthropic does not sell something literally named the Claude Software Factory. But look at the direction of travel. Claude Code is no longer just a completion engine. It can inspect repositories, run tools, execute tests, coordinate work, and operate software. Anthropic now documents separate containment architectures for Claude Code, Claude.ai, and Cowork because capable agents need meaningful access to real systems. My read is that model providers would prefer to give companies a button that says “ship,” not a box of agent parts they must integrate themselves. The better the integrated environment, the more context the agent accumulates and the more useful it becomes. That creates a strong product advantage. It also creates lock-in. The result will not be one universal factory. We are likely to see several patterns: Vendor factories that combine a model, agent harness, execution environment, and deployment workflow. Multi-harness factories that can choose different agents and models for different jobs. Bespoke factories built around a company’s existing CI, platform, security, and incident systems. Packaged private factories that include the hardware required to run local models. flowchart TD E[Production context] --> V[Vendor factory] E --> M[Multi-harness factory] E --> B[Bespoke factory] E --> P[Private factory] V --> R[Reliability gate] M --> R B --> R P --> R Warp represents the multi-harness version. Its definition of a cloud software factory covers the loop from triage through specification, implementation, review, verification, shipping, and monitoring . Warp’s Oz control plane can run Claude Code, Codex, and Warp Agent under shared governance and audit controls . TechCrunch described its latest incarnation as an out-of-the-box software factory for AI development . AMD, Supermicro, and Spectro Cloud take the idea further. Their AMD Instinct Coder packages EPYC processors, eight Instinct GPUs, Pensando networking, a Supermicro server, Spectro Cloud orchestration, and local-first model routing into one enterprise AI coding system. The factory is not merely an agent workflow. It arrives with a bill of materials. This feels like the early web. Every company once assembled its own hosting, build scripts, deployment process, CDN, and rollback machinery. Platforms such as Netlify eventually standardized much of that path. Software factories will probably follow a similar arc: experimentation first, recognizable patterns next, packaged platforms after that. But standardizing the factory does not standardize the product being built. A vendor can package an agent, a runner, and a deployment button. It cannot automatically know your customers, failure history, dependencies, risk tolerance, or definition of correct behavior. A factory that generates the code, generates the test, and grades its own work is a closed loop in the worst sense. Reliability engineering must provide the outside evidence. Close the reliability loop The Reliability Engineer should not become the person who owns every bug. That would recreate the QA silo with a better title and a pager. The role should own the feedback system across whichever factory pattern the company adopts: Production failures become reproducible tests. Customer traffic becomes pre-production validation data. SLOs become release criteria, not dashboard decoration. Incident reviews update agent instructions, tests, and guardrails. Agents receive scoped access to the context required for the task, with audit trails and least-privilege controls. Quality engineers, developers, and operators share evidence instead of handing off tickets. flowchart LR O[Observe] --> R[Reproduce] R --> C[Change] C --> V[Verify] V --> D[Deploy] D --> O Traffic replay is one practical example. Speedscale’s AI code verification workflow can capture real inbound and outbound application traffic and replay a production snapshot against a local development environment . That turns a production observation into a deterministic pre-production check. The same evidence can help a human reproduce a failure or help an agent verify its proposed fix. The product is less important than the pattern: observe, reproduce, change, verify, and feed the result back into the system. Quality is an engineering system Dropping “Site” from SRE will not fix software quality. Neither will renaming QA, buying an agent, or adding another gate to CI. But the title change captures the stance we need. Reliability is not a production specialty. It is the discipline that connects production truth to engineering decisions before and after release. As software factories become products, that discipline matters even more. Factories standardize how changes move. Reliability determines whether those changes deserve to move at all. We spent a decade trying to shift quality left. AI gives us a better option: remove the boundary. Drop the site. Keep the accountability.

title: Best SAT Prep Resources for the Digital SAT: 2026 Guide
summary: Discover the Best SAT Prep Resources for 2026—official Bluebook, Khan Academy, AI-guided tools, and books—plus stacks by level. Start your plan.
body_text: Best SAT Prep Resources for the Digital SAT: 2026 Guide TL;DR The best SAT prep resources are not a single app or book. They are a combination of official College Board tools for realism, a guided platform for daily study, and targeted drills or books for weak areas. Start with Bluebook and Khan Academy (both free), then add an AI-guided platform like Miyagi Labs for diagnostics, personalized practice, and score tracking. Pay for premium question banks or tutoring only after you know exactly what free resources are failing to provide. Direct Answer If you only use three SAT prep resources in 2026, make them these: 1. College Board Bluebook for official Digital SAT practice tests. 2. Khan Academy for free concept learning. 3. An adaptive study platform like Miyagi Labs for personalized practice, diagnostics, and progress tracking. Students targeting 1500+ scores should also add official Student Question Bank practice and targeted books such as Erica Meltzer or College Panda. Most students do not need expensive tutoring until they have exhausted free official resources. Quick Picks: Best SAT Prep Resources by Need Before comparing everything in detail, here are the top picks by category: Best all-in-one AI-guided platform: Miyagi Labs Best official practice: College Board Bluebook + Student Question Bank Best free lessons: Khan Academy Best free live tutoring: Schoolhouse.world Best extra free AI practice: Google Gemini Best premium explanations: UWorld Best budget self-paced course: Magoosh Best structured course with guarantee: PrepScholar Best traditional live class: Princeton Review / Kaplan Best books for targeted mastery: Erica Meltzer, College Panda, 1600.io Build your SAT study plan with a diagnostic, personalized path, and AI-guided practice. Best SAT Prep Resources at a Glance If You Want... Best Choice Official SAT practice Bluebook Free SAT prep Khan Academy Personalized AI study plan Miyagi Labs Live tutoring Schoolhouse.world Detailed explanations UWorld SAT Math book College Panda SAT Reading book Erica Meltzer Budget course Magoosh Live classes Princeton Review Last-minute prep Kaplan Bootcamp At-a-Glance Comparison Table Resource Starting Price Best For Main Strength Digital SAT Realism Main Limitation Miyagi Labs Free practice tests; paid plans from $14.99/mo AI-guided all-in-one prep Diagnostic + personalized path + AI tutor + score predictor High Newer brand, smaller review footprint College Board Bluebook Free Everyone Official test-maker content Highest Finite tests, limited explanations Khan Academy Free Fundamentals and mid-score students Free official video lessons Medium-high Plateaus for 1450+ scorers Schoolhouse.world Free Live accountability Small-group peer tutoring Medium-high Scheduling, peer tutor variability Google Gemini Free Extra practice after Bluebook AI explanations and study plans Medium Not official College Board content UWorld From $59 Premium explanations Detailed illustrated answer breakdowns High Expensive for beginners Magoosh $129 Budget self-paced study Video lessons + score prediction Medium-high Less personalization than AI/tutor PrepScholar $397 Structured weekly plans 160-point guarantee Medium-high Rigid, mixed user sentiment Princeton Review From $299 Traditional live classes Brand recognition, live options Medium Expensive, accuracy concerns Kaplan From $640 (promo) Short bootcamps Cram-friendly schedule Medium Cost, generic instruction Meltzer / College Panda / 1600.io From ~$24 Subject-specific mastery Deep skill-level content Low (simulation), high (skills) No analytics, no adaptive practice How We Evaluated These SAT Prep Resources To rank each SAT prep resource fairly, we compared them across the factors that matter most for Digital SAT success. Evaluation Criteria Factor Why It Matters Official accuracy How closely the questions resemble the real SAT Adaptive practice Mimics the Digital SAT format Explanation quality Helps students learn from mistakes Analytics Tracks weaknesses by skill Full-length tests Builds endurance Mobile access Supports daily practice Value for money Cost versus features Student reputation Feedback from Reddit and independent reviews This article prioritizes resources that improve long-term score gains rather than simply offering the largest question bank. How to Choose the Right SAT Prep Resources Most SAT prep articles rank resources as if every student needs the same thing. That misses the point entirely. The Digital SAT has two sections : Reading and Writing (64 minutes, 54 questions) and Math (70 minutes, 44 questions). Each section uses two modules, and the second module adapts based on your first-module performance. Total testing time is 2 hours and 14 minutes. Every prep resource you use should account for this adaptive, screen-based format. A strong 2026 prep plan covers six jobs: Baseline diagnosis. Find your current score and weakest domains before studying anything. The mistake: jumping into random drills before knowing where your points are hiding. Official accuracy. Learn the real test style through College Board materials. The mistake: burning all official tests in week one or retaking them for inflated scores. Skill instruction. Actually learn the grammar rules, math concepts, and reading strategies you are missing. The mistake: watching lessons passively without timed practice. Targeted drilling. Fix repeatable weaknesses with focused question sets. The mistake: taking full-length test after full-length test instead of drilling specific error patterns. Feedback and explanations. Understand why each mistake happened. The mistake: marking answers right or wrong without writing down the reason. Simulation and accountability. Practice timing, stamina, and test-day nerves. The mistake: cramming the night before instead of doing weekly full-length reviews over months. College Board research from May 2025 found that students who completed 1, 2, and 3+ full-length Bluebook practice tests scored roughly 25.7, 45.5, and 61.4 points higher than similar students who completed none. These are associations, not causal proof , but they reinforce what most tutors already know: consistent, realistic practice matters. The best SAT prep resources for your situation depend on which of these six layers is weakest. The reviews below are organized to help you figure that out. Best SAT Prep Resources, Reviewed 1. Miyagi Labs Best for: Students who want one AI-guided system instead of stitching together five separate tools. Pricing: Free practice tests and diagnostic available Paid subscriptions: $14.99 and $39.99 options via iOS in-app purchase Monthly and annual plans available Key features: Diagnostic tests that identify weaknesses by domain, skill, and difficulty Personalized study path that tells you what to study next Large expert-reviewed SAT question bank with filters Full-length digital SAT practice exams with realistic timing 24/7 AI tutor for instant explanations and guided help Score predictor and progress analytics with skill heatmaps Mobile apps for iOS and Android Gamification (streaks, achievements) to keep you consistent Why it stands out: Most resources handle one or two layers of prep well. Miyagi Labs covers the full loop: diagnose weaknesses, assign targeted work, explain mistakes through an AI tutor, simulate full-length tests, and predict your score as you improve. For students overwhelmed by the question “what should I study next?”, that guided workflow is the actual value. Tradeoffs: Newer brand with a smaller public review footprint than Khan Academy or Kaplan Public web pricing is not fully transparent (subscriptions managed through app stores and the platform) Practitioners on Reddit have praised Miyagi for SAT and ACT practice, though one r/ACT commenter criticized some questions as less accurate, a reminder that AI-powered content needs ongoing quality assurance Verdict: Miyagi Labs is the strongest option for students who want diagnostics, a study plan, explanations, and full-length practice in one place. Still use Bluebook for official test-day realism. Take a free SAT practice exam to see where you stand before building your study plan. 2. College Board Bluebook + Student Question Bank Best for: Every SAT student, period. This is the official practice from the test maker. Pricing: Free Key features: Official full-length digital practice tests in the Bluebook app Timed and scored like the real SAT My Practice dashboard for reviewing scores and analyzing performance Tailored Practice Questions generated from your results Student Question Bank with thousands of official questions filterable by section, domain, skill, and difficulty Why it stands out: Nothing matches the fidelity of the test maker’s own materials. Bluebook uses the same interface and adaptive format you will see on test day. The Student Question Bank gives you official questions you can filter by exactly the skills you need to work on. Tradeoffs: Official full-length tests are finite, and retaking them becomes a memory exercise since questions stay the same Explanations and analytics are limited compared with AI platforms or paid question banks Not a full curriculum, so it will not teach you the concepts behind your mistakes Practitioners on Reddit consistently treat Bluebook as the closest thing to the real exam. A common 2026 complaint is that students run out of official practice tests and then scramble for realistic alternatives. One user warned that retaking a Bluebook test inflates your confidence because you remember the questions. Verdict: Bluebook is non-negotiable. Do not replace it. Build everything else around it. 3. Khan Academy Best for: Building foundations and filling content gaps for free. Pricing: 100% free Key features: Official Digital SAT Math and Reading & Writing courses Video lessons, practice questions, hints, and test-taking tips Web and mobile access Self-paced, self-directed learning Important note: Khan Academy retired the older Official SAT Practice experience at the end of 2023. You can no longer connect a College Board account or import scores into Khan. The current Digital SAT courses are still useful for content learning, but they work differently than the old integrated experience. Why it stands out: Khan is the best free option for students who need to learn or relearn grammar rules, algebra, data analysis, or reading comprehension strategies. It is College Board’s official free prep partner, which means the content aligns with what appears on the actual test. Tradeoffs: Not a full-length testing platform Self-directed with no built-in accountability Less useful once a student already knows the content and needs hard, test-style drilling One Reddit user in July 2026 said Khan is strong for basics but stops being useful around 1450+. Another commenter recommended it specifically for students around the 1200 range, suggesting they target weak topics rather than completing the entire course blindly. Multiple threads converge on the same point: Khan is excellent for learning, but it is not enough on its own for students chasing 1500+. Verdict: Use Khan Academy to learn concepts. Use Bluebook, Miyagi, or UWorld to prove you can perform under test conditions. 4. Schoolhouse.world Best for: Free live accountability and small-group tutoring. Pricing: Free Key features: Free SAT tutoring sessions over Zoom Four-week bootcamps with two 75-minute sessions per week Up to 10 learners per cohort Separate Reading & Writing and Math bootcamps Standalone 75-minute focus sessions Peer tutors who scored in the top 5% on the section they teach Why it stands out: For students who procrastinate with self-study tools or cannot afford a private tutor, Schoolhouse fills a gap that no app can. It provides real human interaction, a schedule to follow, and guided review of official SAT content. College Board announced the Schoolhouse partnership in February 2026. Tradeoffs: Peer tutor quality varies Scheduling constraints (sessions fill up) Best suited for students scoring roughly 400 to 690 in a section, not advanced strategy seekers Students still need independent practice outside sessions One Reddit thread from March 2026 asked whether Schoolhouse’s free bootcamp is enough on its own. The answer: treat it as your accountability and review layer, not a complete replacement for personal drilling and full-length practice. Verdict: Schoolhouse is the best free accountability resource. Pair it with Bluebook and a personal error log. 5. Google Gemini SAT Practice Best for: Extra free full-length practice after you have used up official Bluebook tests. Pricing: Free in the Gemini app Key features: Full-length, on-demand SAT practice exams Built in partnership with The Princeton Review and other education companies Immediate performance feedback and answer explanations Customized study plan based on your results Launched January 2026 with SAT as the first supported test Why it stands out: Students consistently complain about running out of official Bluebook tests. Gemini offers a free, low-friction way to get more full-length practice with AI-powered explanations and study plans. A Reddit user in May 2026 said Gemini’s free tests are “very close” to the real thing and can be generated repeatedly. Tradeoffs: Not official College Board content AI explanations should be double-checked against trusted rules Unknown score predictiveness compared with Bluebook Can encourage volume over quality if students take test after test without reviewing mistakes Verdict: Gemini is a promising free supplement, but it should not replace Bluebook or careful mistake analysis. Use it after official tests, not instead of them. 6. UWorld Best for: Students who learn best by studying detailed answer explanations. Pricing: SAT Study Guide from $59, Question Bank from $99 , SAT Prep Course from $299 Key features: 1,650+ Digital SAT-style practice questions Detailed illustrated explanations for every question Digital-style practice environment Progress analytics and performance tracking Practice tests included in higher tiers Why it stands out: UWorld’s explanations are the real product. Where many platforms tell you the right answer, UWorld walks you through why each wrong answer is wrong and why the right answer works. For students in the 1300 to 1500 range who keep making the same types of mistakes, this depth matters. Tradeoffs: More expensive than free alternatives Not a substitute for official Bluebook test simulation Value depends on how carefully you actually read the explanations Reddit users note the English question bank is thinner than the math side Practitioners on Reddit repeatedly praise UWorld’s explanations, especially for math. One user called it expensive but high quality, recommending it primarily after running out of official Question Bank questions. Verdict: UWorld is one of the strongest paid upgrades when your problem is not “I need lessons” but “I need better questions with better explanations.” If you want to focus on targeted SAT problem sets by skill, consider pairing UWorld’s explanations with a platform that tracks your weak domains. 7. Magoosh Best for: Budget-conscious students who want a structured self-paced course under $150. Pricing: Premium at $129 for 12 months, Premium + On-Demand Classes at $399. Includes a 7-day trial and 100-point guarantee. Key features: 200+ video lessons Practice questions with explanations Study schedules for different timelines Score prediction tool Email support from tutors Mobile-friendly access Why it stands out: Magoosh occupies a useful middle ground: more structured than Khan Academy, far cheaper than Kaplan or Princeton Review. The study schedules help students who need someone to say “do this today, then this tomorrow.” Tradeoffs: Less official content fidelity than Bluebook Less explanation depth than UWorld for some question types Less personalization than an AI-guided platform Requires self-discipline to stick with the schedule A parent on Reddit in May 2026 said Khan was the easiest starting point because it was free, but Magoosh became more useful than expected because their child found it organized and easier to stick with over time. Verdict: Magoosh is a solid budget upgrade when Khan feels too loose and full tutoring is too expensive. 8. PrepScholar Best for: Students who want a rigid weekly plan and a score-improvement guarantee. Pricing: Self-paced at $397 for 12 months, live classes at $895. Includes a 160-point improvement guarantee and a 5-day trial. Key features: 90+ skill lessons 4,100+ realistic practice questions Smart diagnostic Customized weekly prep schedule AI Learning Assistant option Why it stands out: PrepScholar’s guarantee (160 points or your money back) appeals to families who want a safety net. The structured weekly plan removes the guesswork of what to study when. Tradeoffs: The guarantee requires completing all assigned lessons and tests, plus meeting specific score-report conditions Rigid plans frustrate students who want more control $397 is a significant investment that is wasted if the student does not follow through Reddit sentiment is mixed: one user said they “hated it” but admitted procrastination was part of the problem Verdict: PrepScholar works best for families buying structure and accountability, not for students who resist assigned coursework. 9. The Princeton Review Best for: Families who want traditional live classes or private tutoring from a recognized brand. Pricing: Self-paced from $299, SAT Essentials at $649, SAT 1400+ at $1,849, private tutoring at $376/hour Key features: Self-paced, live online, and in-person course options Private tutoring packages Score guarantees on select packages Practice tests, drills, videos, and study guides Why it stands out: Princeton Review has decades of brand recognition and offers the widest range of formats: self-paced, group class, and one-on-one tutoring. For families who want a formal class schedule with a recognizable name, it checks the boxes. Tradeoffs: Expensive at higher tiers (tutoring packages can exceed $7,000) Practitioners on Reddit question the accuracy of Princeton Review practice tests, noting they differ from the real SAT in difficulty and question logic Guarantees have strict completion conditions One Reddit thread from June 2026 suggested the 1500+ program is often not worth the money Verdict: Princeton Review makes sense for families who want live instruction, but students should still validate their readiness with Bluebook and official questions. 10. Kaplan Best for: Students with a near test date who need a fast, structured bootcamp. Pricing: Bootcamp from $799 (discounted to $640 during promotions), Live Online Plus at $1,099, tutoring packages from $1,999 to $2,999 Key features: 18 hours of live online bootcamp instruction 35 on-demand strategy and content video lessons Adaptive digital practice tests 2 to 3 week compressed timeline Unlimited prep package covering SAT, ACT, PSAT, and AP Why it stands out: Kaplan’s bootcamp is designed for students who are weeks, not months, from test day. The compressed schedule forces a study rhythm that self-paced tools struggle to create. Tradeoffs: Expensive compared with nearly every other option on this list Bootcamps compress prep, which is not ideal for students with major content gaps Reddit users caution that Kaplan practice tests may not predict real SAT scores accurately Brand-name classes can feel generic if you need personalized diagnostics Verdict: Kaplan is a reasonable accountability purchase for students who need a fast schedule. But it should not replace official practice and personalized error review. If you want to check your predicted score before committing to an expensive bootcamp, a free diagnostic can tell you whether you need content learning or just test simulation. 11. Erica Meltzer, College Panda, and 1600.io Best for: Targeted subject mastery when you know exactly which section is dragging your score down. Pricing: College Panda SAT Math at ~$24, Erica Meltzer books vary by retailer (typically $25 to $35), 1600.io Premium membership includes 5,000+ explanatory videos and the SAT Math Orange Book Key features: Erica Meltzer: Deep grammar rules, reading strategy, and verbal reasoning for Reading & Writing College Panda: Concept-driven SAT Math with workbook-style practice 1600.io: Video walkthroughs of official SAT problems, Desmos graph explanations, and the SAT Math Orange Book Why it stands out: These are surgical tools. Reddit users aiming for 1500+ consistently recommend 1600.io for math and Erica Meltzer for English. One student who scored 1600 credited the 1600.io SAT Math Orange Book as the resource that “helped a lot” after starting with Khan Academy. Tradeoffs: Books do not simulate the adaptive Digital SAT No automatic analytics, no AI tutor, no reminders Students must pair books with Bluebook or a digital practice platform Not useful for students who do not yet know which section needs work Verdict: Books are best as precision instruments. Use them when you have already identified the weak section. Do not use them as your only Digital SAT practice. Which SAT Prep Resource Is Best for Your Score Goal? Goal Recommended Stack 1000→1200 Khan + Bluebook 1200→1350 Khan + Miyagi + Bluebook 1350→1450 Miyagi + UWorld + Question Bank 1450+ Bluebook + Question Bank + Meltzer + 1600.io Best SAT Prep Resources by Student Type Beginners (under 1100): Start with Khan Academy for content learning, take a Bluebook diagnostic to find your weakest domains, and use a guided platform like Miyagi Labs to build a daily study habit. Do not buy expensive courses yet. Mid-range students (1100 to 1300): This is where the biggest point gains happen. Use Miyagi or Khan for targeted skill work, the Student Question Bank for official practice by domain, and take one full-length Bluebook test every one to two weeks. Focus on fixing major gaps before worrying about advanced strategy. High scorers (1300 to 1450): You need targeted drilling and explanation depth, not more broad lessons. Use UWorld or official hard questions, keep an error log, and track which question types cost you the most points. SAT practice by skill becomes more valuable than generic full-length tests at this stage. Elite scorers (1450+): High scorers lose points on a handful of question types, not broad content. Use official hard questions, Bluebook for timing practice, Erica Meltzer or 1600.io for surgical gaps, and AI or tutor feedback for the mistakes that keep recurring. One month left: Take one full-length test per week. Do daily weak-domain drills. Get explanations (AI or tutor) for every miss. Do not start a giant new course in your final week. Cannot afford paid prep: The free stack is genuinely powerful: Bluebook, Student Question Bank, Khan Academy, Schoolhouse.world, and Google Gemini. Add a personal error log (even a spreadsheet works) and you have more than enough to improve significantly. Need accountability: Schoolhouse bootcamps (free), Magoosh study schedules (budget), or Kaplan/Princeton Review live classes (premium) all provide external structure. An AI-guided platform with streaks and reminders can also help. Free vs. Paid SAT Prep: When Should You Pay? Do not pay until you know what free resources are failing to provide. Pay when: You need a guided plan instead of self-directed browsing You need explanations beyond what Khan Academy offers You have exhausted official free questions and need more realistic practice You need analytics and a score predictor to measure progress You are losing the same question types repeatedly and need targeted drills You need mobile study with reminders to stay consistent Do not pay when: You have not taken a diagnostic yet You have not used Bluebook, Khan, or the Student Question Bank You are hoping a course will replace consistency You will not review your mistakes The hidden costs of SAT prep add up quickly. The SAT itself costs $68 to register in the U.S. through December 2026. Retakes cost money unless you qualify for fee waivers. Live tutoring can run $1,000 to $7,000+. Score-improvement guarantees require strict completion conditions. And some app trials auto-convert to paid subscriptions if you forget to cancel. Suggested SAT Prep Stacks The Free Stack Bluebook for official full-length tests Student Question Bank for domain-specific official practice Khan Academy for content learning Schoolhouse.world for live support Google Gemini for extra practice and AI explanations A personal error log The AI-Guided Stack Miyagi Labs diagnostic to find your starting point Miyagi personalized study path for daily work Bluebook for official checkpoints every two weeks Miyagi AI tutor for instant mistake explanations Student Question Bank for official hard questions The High-Score Stack Bluebook for timing and simulation Student Question Bank, filtered to hard questions UWorld for detailed explanations Erica Meltzer for Reading & Writing precision 1600.io or College Panda for Math depth Analytics tracking to monitor improvement over time The Last-Month Stack One full-length Bluebook test per week Daily weak-domain problem sets AI or tutor explanations for every missed question No new courses, no cramming new content Sleep Prep Timeline Quick Guide Time Until Test What to Focus On 6 months Diagnostic, content learning, weekly drills, monthly full-length tests 3 months Guided plan, targeted problem sets, one full-length every 1 to 2 weeks 1 month Bluebook simulation, error log, weak-domain drilling, explanations for every miss 1 week Light review, timing practice, formulas and grammar rules, rest For additional SAT prep resources and study guides, check out more tools organized by test section and skill level. FAQ What is the best SAT prep resource overall? There is no single best resource. The best SAT prep resources work together as a stack. Start with College Board Bluebook for official practice (free), add Khan Academy for content learning (free), and use an AI-guided platform like Miyagi Labs for diagnostics, targeted drilling, explanations, and score prediction. Add UWorld, books, or tutoring only when you have identified a specific gap that free tools are not fixing. Is Khan Academy enough for SAT prep? Khan Academy is excellent for foundations and mid-range scorers, but it is rarely enough on its own for students targeting 1450+. Reddit users consistently report that Khan works best for learning content up to about the 1300 range. After that, students need harder official questions, detailed explanations, and test-simulation practice that Khan does not provide. Are Bluebook practice tests the most accurate? Yes. Bluebook tests are made by College Board, the organization that creates the actual SAT. No third-party test can match that fidelity. College Board research found that students who completed 3+ Bluebook practice tests scored roughly 61 points higher than similar students who took none. What should I use after finishing all Bluebook tests? This is one of the most common questions on Reddit. Your best options are: the Student Question Bank (official, filterable by skill and difficulty), Google Gemini’s free practice tests for additional full-length practice, UWorld for premium questions with detailed explanations, and Miyagi Labs for full-length digital practice exams with score prediction. Save at least two official Bluebook tests for the final three to four weeks before your test date. Are paid SAT prep courses worth it? It depends entirely on what you need. If you are disciplined and the free stack (Bluebook, Khan, Student Question Bank, Schoolhouse) is working, paid courses may not add much. Paid resources become worth it when you need a guided study plan, better explanations, more realistic practice questions, or accountability. A $129 Magoosh subscription or a Miyagi Labs plan will often deliver more value per dollar than a $2,000+ tutoring package. Is AI SAT prep reliable? AI-powered prep tools are useful for explanations, study plans, and on-demand help. They are riskier when students blindly trust AI-generated questions or scoring without cross-checking against official materials. The strongest approach: use AI inside a structured prep workflow (like Miyagi Labs) for explanations and guided practice, but always validate your readiness with official Bluebook tests. What is the best SAT prep book? For Reading & Writing, Erica Meltzer’s guides are the most recommended by high scorers on Reddit. For Math, College Panda (about $24) and the 1600.io SAT Math Orange Book are the top choices. Books work best as surgical tools for known weak areas, not as your only form of Digital SAT practice. How many SAT practice tests should I take? College Board data suggests that 3+ full-length practice tests is the threshold where score gains become most significant. A good rule: take one at the start for a baseline, one every one to two weeks during active prep, and at least two official Bluebook tests in the final month. Reviewing every missed question matters more than the raw number of tests you complete. Start targeted SAT practice to identify your weakest skills and build a study plan around them.

title: ZenaTech Closes 27th Drone as a Service Acquisition Expanding into Idaho, Strengthening Drone-Based Surveying and Civil Engineering Services for Government and Construction Customers
summary: ZenaTech Closes 27th Drone as a Service Acquisition Expanding into Idaho, Strengthening Drone-Based Surveying and Civil Engineering Services for Government […]
body_text: Vancouver, British Columbia, (August 6, 2026) — ZenaTech, Inc. (Nasdaq: ZENA) (FSE: 49Q) (BMV: ZENA) (“ZenaTech”), a technology solution provider specializing in AI (Artificial Intelligence) drone, Drone as a Service (DaaS), enterprise SaaS, and Quantum Computing solutions, announces that it has completed the acquisition of Ketchum, Idaho-based Benchmark Partners LLC, doing business as Galena-Benchmark Engineering . The acquired company is a full-service professional civil engineering and land surveying firm with a long history of providing civil engineering, land planning, and land information systems services to an established roster of commercial and government customers. The acquisition marks ZenaTech’s 27th Drone as a Service acquisition to date and its first location in Idaho. “This acquisition expands our Drone as a Service footprint into Idaho, our 13th U.S. state, establishing a strong presence in a market supported by growing construction, agriculture, infrastructure and public sector demand,” said Shaun Passley, Ph.D., CEO of ZenaTech. “With more than 30 years of trusted customer relationships and an established reputation across central and southern Idaho, Galena-Benchmark provides an ideal platform for our acquisition and expansion strategy. We see significant opportunities to broaden its service offerings through drone-enabled surveying, environmental monitoring, precision agriculture, forestry and wildfire management, and utility inspections, creating new recurring revenue opportunities while delivering greater efficiency and value to customers.” Galena-Benchmark Engineering is a full-service, multi-discipline firm with a 30-year background, providing professional services in civil engineering, land planning, surveying, and land information systems in multiple counties across central and southern Idaho. They serve a diversified customer base including municipal and government customers, construction companies, and builders supporting the area’s rapid growth in the public works, tourism and agriculture sectors. The Company plans to offer drone-based land surveying and 3D construction monitoring through its ZenaWorx platform, and future precision agriculture, forestry and land management, utility inspections, wildfire mitigation and environmental monitoring. Management believes Idaho’s growing economy and demand for technology-driven solutions will support recurring drone services that improve speed, efficiency, analytics, data and safety needs for customers across the state. ZenaTech’s Drone as a Service platform provides business and government customers with on-demand and subscription-based drone services using its own ZenaDrone product platforms, for a host of surveying, inspections, maintenance, power washing, and precision agriculture solutions—eliminating the need for customers to own, operate and maintain commercial-grade drone fleets. Through the acquisition of established, profitable but under digitized service businesses, ZenaTech is building a scalable global DaaS network and AI autonomy platform, with recurring revenue and an existing customer base, while integrating advanced drone technologies to deliver greater speed, precision, safety, and data-driven insights. The Company continues to expand its geographic footprint, service offerings, and drone capabilities to drive long-term growth. About ZenaTech ZenaTech , Inc. (Nasdaq: ZENA) (FSE: 49Q) (BMV: ZENA) is a technology company that specializes in AI autonomy drone platforms to transform commercial, government, and defense sectors. Its subsidiaries include drone manufacturing through ZenaDrone, a global Drone as a Service (DaaS) business, and an enterprise SaaS division of software brands. The Company is executing an acquisition-led DaaS roll-up strategy to digitize and automate legacy service industries including land surveys and inspections, driving drone-based scalable, recurring revenue growth. With an operating footprint spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, ZenaTech is advancing AI drones for agriculture and logistics, as well as ISR, cargo, and counter-UAS applications for U.S. defense and NATO allies. The company is investing in next-generation technologies, including drone swarms, quantum computing, and advanced AI autonomy to capture long-term opportunities in key markets through its R&D initiatives. About ZenaDrone ZenaDrone , a subsidiary of ZenaTech, develops and manufactures AI-powered multifunction autonomous drone solutions integrating machine learning, predictive analytics, and advanced computing technologies, for government, defense, and industrial applications. This includes multifunctional drones for surveying, inspections, logistics, security, and defense applications. Its product portfolio includes the ZenaDrone 1000 for ISR defense and specialized cargo, the IQ Nano for indoor inventory management and security, the IQ Square for outdoor inspections and maintenance, the IQ Quad for land surveying, and the IQ Aqua for underwater applications. ZenaDrone operates three global manufacturing facilities in Arizona, Dubai, and Taiwan, and is advancing counter-UAS maritime interceptor drones and an integrated defense system.
